findings.title: Missing 'Document Quality Gate' log in PR description
findings.body: The spec PR description is empty, violating the REVIEW.md requirement that spec PRs include a current 'Document Quality Gate' log. A missing log is a blocking finding by default per the checklist.

findings.title: No consistency matrix for stateful decision-gate behavior
findings.body: The spec defines complex workflow decision-gate behavior (e.g., sweep enablement logic in AC18, category list validity in AC19, evidence tier transitions). Per REVIEW.md, such PRs must include a consistency matrix or pointer identifying gate inputs, allowed outcomes, required next actions, mirror surfaces, and examples. Its absence is blocking before 'ready-for-human-review'.

findings.title: Missing 'Matrix coherence preflight' audit for stateful contract
findings.body: The spec contains multiple stateful contracts: evidence tier transitions (Statuses / Enum Values), sweep enablement states (AC18), and category list validity conditions (AC19, Business Rules). Per REVIEW.md, the PR's 'Document Quality Gate' log must carry a 'Matrix coherence preflight' row with the six-check audit summary. Its absence — or a row claiming 'Not applicable' when stateful contracts exist — is a blocking misclassification.

findings.title: Contradictory business rule on seeded benchmark's four never-found kinds
findings.body: Business Rules state 'The seeded benchmark's four never-found kinds are not, on their own, a valid basis for the list, because no real-pull-request evidence confirms them' (line 472), but the Statuses / Enum Values section explicitly excludes them 'because unconfirmed by real-PR evidence' (line 481). This creates a contradiction: the rule says they are invalid as a basis, yet the exclusion rationale treats them as a candidate considered and rejected. Both sections must align on whether they were ever eligible for inclusion.

findings.title: Ambiguous threshold for 'Real-PR evidence (measured)'
findings.body: AC15(b) states the 'Real-PR evidence (measured)' tier requires 'at least ten pull requests under the current recorded category list version have been sweep-enabled and reviewed, and their external-finding evidence has been adjudicated'. However, the Evidence tier section (lines 512-515) only mentions 'adjudicated' for the transition to 'measured', not for the initial 'provisional' label. This ambiguity makes it unclear whether 'provisional' applies before any adjudication or only before the tenth adjudication.

findings.title: Inconsistent capitalization of 'dogfooded'
findings.body: The Coverage Matrix (line 651) uses 'dogfooded' while Open Questions (line 771) uses 'dogfooded'. Consistent capitalization ('dogfooded') should be applied throughout per standard English conventions for compound adjectives.

findings.title: Contradictory business rule about current category list validity
findings.body: Business Rules states 'A list with no categories is not a valid current list' (line 379), but the Statuses / Enum Values section states 'While Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved, the recorded list is not a complete AC6 record and cannot be marked current' (line 413) — implying an incomplete list (missing decisions on two candidates) is invalid, while the Business Rule only invalidates empty lists. These conflict: the Business Rule permits a non-empty but incomplete list to be current, while the Statuses section forbids it. Both must align on what makes a list 'current'.

findings.title: AC6 misclassification in Statuses section
findings.body: The Statuses / Enum Values section states 'While Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved, the recorded list is not a complete AC6 record and cannot be marked current' (line 413), but AC6 itself (line 624) requires the list to account for every candidate — including those pending decisions — and explicitly says 'while the spec-AC-compliance and per-finding-resolution outcomes [...] are unresolved, the recorded list cannot be marked current'. This is a correct restatement of AC6, but the Statuses section presents it as a standalone rule rather than a direct consequence of AC6, creating redundancy and risking misinterpretation as an independent constraint. It should instead reference AC6 directly.

findings.title: AC6 contains unstated assumption about human decision timing
findings.body: AC6 states the recorded list 'cannot be marked current' while Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved, but does not specify when the human decision must occur — e.g., before first deployment, before first real-PR review, or before evidence tier promotion. Without this, operators lack guidance on required cadence, risking indefinite 'provisional' status. The Business Rules or Considerations should clarify the decision deadline.

findings.title: AC15(b) threshold definition contradicts Open Question 4 phrasing
findings.body: AC15(b) states 'at least ten pull requests' as the working minimum (line 647), but Open Question 4 (line 823) asks to 'confirm that ten is the gate', implying uncertainty. This creates a contradiction: AC15(b) treats ten as fixed while OQ4 treats it as provisional. Either AC15(b) must be conditional ('subject to OQ4 resolution') or OQ4 must be resolved in the spec.

findings.title: Deferral Note D1 uses informal language inconsistent with spec tone
findings.body: Deferral Note D1 (line 733) uses colloquial phrasing ('yes — confirm that rebalancing stays out of scope for this item') which breaks the formal, imperative style expected in specifications. It should be rephrased as a declarative statement (e.g., 'Rebalancing, re-weighting, or removing existing seeds is deferred to preserve baseline comparability').

findings.title: Contradictory business rule about list validity
findings.body: Business Rules states 'A list with no categories is not a valid current list' (line 574), but the Statuses / Enum Values section shows an initial list with exactly five categories and then states 'While Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved, the recorded list is not a complete AC6 record and cannot be marked current' (line 613). AC6 requires every candidate to be either swept or explicitly excluded, but the spec simultaneously presents a 'current' list that is incomplete per AC6 and declares it invalid per the Business Rule. These two statements contradict: one says no-categories is invalid, the other implies incomplete-but-non-empty is also invalid, yet the document never defines what constitutes a 'valid current list' when candidates are pending.

findings.title: AC6 violation in documented state
findings.body: AC6 requires the recorded list to account for every candidate category, including spec-AC-compliance and per-finding resolution, by placing each either on the swept list or in the excluded list with rationale. The spec explicitly states (line 613) that while Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved, the list 'cannot be marked current' — meaning the documented initial list violates AC6. Since AC6 is a required acceptance criterion and the spec presents this list as the 'initial list', the document contains an unresolvable contradiction: it both exhibits the list and declares it non-compliant with its own AC6.

findings.title: Missing definition of 'current' list version
findings.body: The spec repeatedly references 'exactly one recorded category list version is current' (lines 611, 621, 685) and ties currency to AC4 and AC6 compliance, but never defines what 'current' means operationally or how a version attains or loses that status. The Business Rules section (line 574) says 'Exactly one sweep category list is current at any time', but provides no mechanism, trigger, or authority for marking a version current — only conditions under which it cannot be marked current. This leaves implementers unable to determine when a list version becomes active, violating the requirement for testable acceptance criteria.

findings.title: Inconsistent treatment of 'planted-proof evidence'
findings.body: The Statuses / Enum Values section (line 714) excludes 'Planted-proof evidence' as 'a workflow-gate artifact... not a product defect class', but the Business Rules section (line 589) states 'The seeded benchmark's four never-found kinds are not, on their own, a valid basis for the list, because no real-pull-request evidence confirms them' — implying that workflow artifacts are categorically excluded. However, the spec does not explain why planted-proof evidence is excluded while other workflow artifacts (e.g., spec-AC-compliance, per-finding resolution) are pending human decision. This creates ambiguity about the exclusion principle and risks inconsistent application.

findings.title: Ambiguous 'roughly 10' language in AC15
findings.body: AC15 (line 859) uses 'at least ten' but the Open Questions section (line 972) and Brief Objective List (O11, line 837) refer to 'roughly 10'. The spec must use consistent, testable language: 'at least ten' is precise and verifiable; 'roughly 10' is vague and untestable. Since AC15 is an acceptance criterion, it must be stated with the precision required for verification.

findings.title: Contradictory category list validity requirements
findings.body: The Business Rules section states 'A list with no categories is not a valid current list' (line 121), but the Decision-gate consistency matrix row 'Category list readability (AC19)' states 'Unreadable, empty, or malformed: the sweep does not run...' (line 371) and the AC19 acceptance criterion defines 'empty' as a malformed condition that triggers degradation (line 1023). These conflict: one says an empty list is invalid (and thus presumably prevents the sweep from being current), while the other treats emptiness as a runtime degradation case. The spec must resolve whether an empty list can ever be 'current' or if its existence violates the invariant.

findings.title: Inconsistent 'empty' handling between Business Rules and AC19
findings.body: The Business Rules section (line 121) declares an empty list invalid, yet the AC19 decision gate (line 371) and AC19 itself (line 1023) explicitly treat 'empty' as a condition that triggers degradation to non-sweep behavior. This creates a contradiction: if an empty list is invalid, it should prevent the list from being 'current' at all, making the degradation path unreachable. The spec must align these definitions—either empty lists are prohibited from becoming current (requiring validation at list publication time), or the Business Rule's 'not valid' statement is inaccurate and should be revised to match AC19's operational treatment.

findings.title: AC19 malformation definition contradicts Business Rule on empty lists
findings.body: AC19 (line 1023) explicitly includes 'empty' in its list of malformation conditions that trigger the 'sweep did not run' degradation, while the Business Rules section (line 121) states 'A list with no categories is not a valid current list'. These are incompatible: if an empty list cannot be 'current', then the AC19 degradation path for emptiness would never execute. The spec must reconcile this by either removing 'empty' from AC19's malformation list (if emptiness is caught earlier) or revising the Business Rule to acknowledge that emptiness is a recoverable runtime condition, not an invalid state.

findings.title: Decision-gate matrix omits critical 'not determined' outcome handling
findings.body: The Decision-gate consistency matrix row 'Pass-outcome surface assignment (AC1)' (line 433) describes surface assignment for 'pre-review skip', 'reached completion', and 'terminal failure after review execution', but fails to explicitly name or define the 'not determined' outcome state introduced in AC1 (line 741). While AC1 details when 'not determined' applies (terminal failure after review execution but before finding result establishment), the matrix should enumerate it as a distinct outcome with its own surface assignment rule to ensure consistency across documentation surfaces.

findings.title: 'Not determined' outcome scope ambiguity
findings.body: AC1 (line 741) defines 'not determined' as applying only when 'the failure occurs before the review is already public', but later clarifies that failures 'after the review is already public' use ordinary produced-findings/produced-none values. However, the boundary between 'before public' and 'already public' is undefined—publication is asynchronous and may involve multiple steps (e.g., GitHub API call, retry logic). The spec should clarify the precise technical condition (e.g., 'before the review creation API call succeeds') that determines when 'not determined' applies.

findings.title: Contradictory list readability behavior
findings.body: The Business Rules section states that when the sweep is enabled and the current category list cannot be read, or is empty or malformed, 'the pass proceeds as an ordinary non-sweep review and records that the sweep did not run' (line 120). However, AC19 (line 1412) states that in this case, 'a pass that reaches review execution preserves the ordinary publication eligibility (AC2) — it publishes its normal review for that head only when the existing review flow reaches publication — and records that the sweep did not run'. These are contradictory: the Business Rules say the pass proceeds as a non-sweep review, while AC19 says it preserves publication eligibility. The spec must resolve whether the pass behaves identically to a non-sweep review (including no per-category record) or whether it retains sweep-specific behaviors like recording 'sweep-did-not-run' while publishing normally.

findings.title: Contradictory list readability behavior
findings.body: The Business Rules section states that when the sweep is enabled and the current category list cannot be read, or is empty or malformed, 'the pass proceeds as an ordinary non-sweep review and records that the sweep did not run' (line 120). However, AC19 (line 1412) states that in this case, 'a pass that reaches review execution preserves the ordinary publication eligibility (AC2) — it publishes its normal review for that head only when the existing review flow reaches publication — and records that the sweep did not run'. These are contradictory: the Business Rules say the pass proceeds as a non-sweep review, while AC19 says it preserves publication eligibility. The spec must resolve whether the pass behaves identically to a non-sweep review (including no per-category record) or whether it retains sweep-specific behaviors like recording 'sweep-did-not-run' while publishing normally.

findings.title: Ambiguous 'sweep-did-not-run' record surface
findings.body: The Business Rules state that when the sweep is enabled but the list is unreadable/empty/malformed, the pass 'records that the sweep did not run' (line 127), but do not specify where this record appears. AC19 (line 1412) clarifies it goes on 'the surfaces AC1 assigns to the pass's outcome', yet AC1 (line 1301) defines those surfaces conditionally based on whether a check run was published. This creates ambiguity: if the pass publishes a review (so its check run outcome is a review), does the 'sweep-did-not-run' record appear in both the check-run output and logs? Or only in one? The spec must explicitly define the surface(s) for this record.

findings.title: Inconsistent 'reaching review execution' definition
findings.body: AC1 (line 1301) defines 'reaching review execution' as 'the pass reads the changed files and runs the review', but the Business Rules section (line 120) uses the same phrase without defining it. Later in AC1 (line 1313), it clarifies that 'reaching review execution' means the pass reads the changed files and runs the review, yet the Business Rules section (line 120) references this boundary without linking to the definition. This creates risk of inconsistent interpretation between sections. The spec must either define the term in the Business Rules section or add a cross-reference to AC1's definition.

findings.title: Inconsistent 'reaching review execution' definition
findings.body: AC1 (line 1301) defines 'reaching review execution' as 'the pass reads the changed files and runs the review', but the Business Rules section (line 120) uses the same phrase without defining it. Later in AC1 (line 1313), it clarifies that 'reaching review execution' means the pass reads the changed files and runs the review, yet the Business Rules section (line 120) references this boundary without linking to the definition. This creates risk of inconsistent interpretation between sections. The spec must either define the term in the Business Rules section or add a cross-reference to AC1's definition.

findings.title: Contradictory list readability requirements
findings.body: The Business Rules section states 'If the current category list cannot be read, or is empty or malformed... the pass proceeds as an ordinary non-sweep review' (lines 119-122), but AC19 defines 'malformed' to include cases where 'any category lacks a display label, a description, a failure shape, an evidence source, an identifier, or a finding-instance count' (lines 1483-1485). However, the initial list in Statuses/Enum Values shows the 'credential-pattern-gap' category with evidence source text spanning two lines (lines 374-375) which violates AC19's requirement for evidence source to be 'a non-empty string that is not blank'. This creates a contradiction where the spec both requires the list to be readable and defines the current list as malformed.

findings.title: Malformed evidence source violates AC19
findings.body: AC19 requires each category's evidence source to be 'a non-empty string that is not blank', but the 'credential-pattern-gap' category's evidence source spans two lines (lines 374-375) with line continuation, making it invalid per AC19's definition of malformed. This renders the current list unreadable per AC19, contradicting the spec's requirement that the list be current and usable.

findings.title: AC19 malformed definition contradicts list implementation
findings.body: AC19 defines 'malformed' to include 'any category lacks a display label, a description, a failure shape, an evidence source, an identifier, or a finding-instance count', but the initial list implements 'credential-pattern-gap' with a multi-line evidence source (lines 374-375) that cannot be parsed as a single non-empty string per AC19's requirements. This makes the spec internally inconsistent as it presents a list that fails its own validity criteria.

findings.title: Contradictory list readability behavior
findings.body: The Business Rules section states that when the sweep is enabled and the current category list cannot be read, or is empty or malformed, 'the pass proceeds as an ordinary non-sweep review and records that the sweep did not run' (line 120). However, AC19 (line 1443) states that in this case 'a pass that reaches review execution preserves the ordinary publication eligibility (AC2) — it publishes its normal review for that head only when the existing review flow reaches publication — and records that the sweep did not run'. These are contradictory: the Business Rules claim the pass 'proceeds as an ordinary non-sweep review', while AC19 says it preserves 'ordinary publication eligibility' but does not state it proceeds as a non-sweep review. The spec must resolve whether the degraded pass runs the full non-sweep logic (including all its categories) or simply skips the sweep and publishes the same findings as a non-sweep review would have.

findings.title: Missing definition of 'malformed' list
findings.body: AC19 (line 1443) defines a malformed list as including cases where 'any category lacks a display label, a description, a failure shape, an evidence source, an identifier, or a finding-instance count (AC4), or supplies any of those as a value outside its allowed domain'. However, AC4 (line 1372) does not define the 'allowed domain' for these fields — it only requires they be present. The spec fails to specify what constitutes an invalid display label, description, etc., making the 'malformed' condition untestable. This violates the checklist requirement that business rules be unambiguous and non-contradictory.

findings.title: Undefined 'allowed domain' for category fields
findings.body: AC4 (line 1372) requires each category to state 'its identifier, display label, description, the failure shape it targets, supporting real-pull-request evidence source, and finding-instance count' but does not define the 'allowed domain' for any of these fields. This makes the category list validation impossible to implement or test. The spec must explicitly define valid formats, character sets, length limits, and other constraints for each field to satisfy the checklist requirement that business rules be unambiguous.

findings.title: Contradictory version reporting behavior
findings.body: AC19 (line 1443) states that when the category list is unreadable, empty, or malformed, 'the pass reports no list version as used'. However, the Business Rules section (line 124) states that in this case 'the pass proceeds as an ordinary non-sweep review and records that the sweep did not run'. These conflict on whether the pass should record 'sweep-did-not-run' (Business Rules) or 'no list version as used' (AC19). The spec must reconcile these and clarify what exact record is produced in the degraded case.

findings.title: Inconsistent error handling for list parsing failures
findings.body: AC19 (line 1443) lists multiple conditions for a 'malformed' list (e.g., missing fields, invalid counts, duplicate identifiers) but does not specify how each condition maps to distinct error outcomes or logging. The spec requires 'the pass reports no list version as used' for all malformed cases, but fails to distinguish between recoverable parsing errors (e.g., whitespace-only field) and fatal structural errors (e.g., invalid JSON). This violates the checklist requirement that stateful contracts be fully specified with clear transitions and outcomes.

findings.title: Missing consistency matrix for decision-gate behavior
findings.body: The spec introduces four new decision gates (sweep enablement resolution, category list readability, pass-outcome surface assignment, evidence-tier transition, claim admissibility) but the 'Decision-gate consistency matrix' section only documents five gates. The review checklist requires a consistency matrix or pointer for every complex workflow decision-gate behavior. The matrix is present but incomplete: it lists five gates while the text states 'four decision gates and one pass-outcome rule'. The matrix must either document exactly the four gates plus the pass-outcome rule, or explicitly explain why a fifth gate appears. Without this, implementers cannot verify correct gate behavior.

findings.title: Inconsistent gate count in consistency matrix
findings.body: The 'Decision-gate consistency matrix' section header states 'This feature adds four decision gates and one pass-outcome rule', but the table contains five rows labeled as 'Gate'. This contradicts the header and creates ambiguity about whether there are four or five normative decision points. The spec must resolve this inconsistency by either correcting the header to match the table (five gates) or adjusting the table to contain exactly four gate rows plus one pass-outcome row, with mirror surfaces updated accordingly.

findings.title: Ambiguous 'per-category pass record' business rule reference
findings.body: The business rule at line 541 references 'AC1' but AC1 is an acceptance criterion, not a business rule. The spec mixes business rule and acceptance criterion numbering, making it unclear whether this is a typo or an intentional cross-reference. Business rules should reference other business rules or clearly state when they depend on acceptance criteria. This ambiguity could lead implementers to misinterpret the authority of the per-category record requirement.

findings.title: Contradictory definition of 'terminal adjudication'
findings.body: The 'Evidence tier' section defines terminal adjudication as requiring outcomes including 'ronda_only' and 'ronda_rejected', but the 'Adjudication outcomes' section states these are 'not values of the adjudication-outcome enum' and exist only as head-level records. This contradiction means the evidence tier's terminal condition cannot be satisfied as written. The spec must reconcile whether 'ronda_only' and 'ronda_rejected' are valid adjudication outcomes for individual findings or only head-level records.

findings.title: Redundant phrase in AC15(d)
findings.body: AC15(d) contains the redundant phrase 'they do not pair the claim.' appearing twice in the same paragraph (lines 1513 and 1521). This repetition creates confusion about whether it's an editorial error or carries semantic weight. The spec should remove the duplicate instance to improve clarity and maintain professional documentation standards.

findings.title: Contradictory category list readability rule
findings.body: The Business Rules section states 'When the sweep is enabled and the current category list cannot be read, or is empty or malformed, at the start of a pass that reaches review execution, the pass proceeds as an ordinary non-sweep review and records that the sweep did not run' (line 120). However, AC19 defines the same condition but adds specific malformedness criteria (e.g., duplicate identifiers, missing fields, zero counts) and states 'In each of these cases the pass reports no list version as used'. The Business Rules section omits these detailed malformedness conditions and the 'no list version' reporting requirement, creating ambiguity about what constitutes 'malformed' and what must be recorded. Both sections must align on the exact failure conditions and required outputs.

findings.title: Missing definition of 'per-category pass record' surfaces
findings.body: The Business Rules section references 'the surfaces AC1 assigns to the pass's outcome' for the per-category pass record (line 541), but AC1's description of surfaces is buried in a dense paragraph with conditional logic about check-run outputs vs. logs. The spec lacks a clear, standalone definition of which surfaces (e.g., 'check-run output', 'logs', 'benchmark output') are the canonical, named surfaces for this record. This makes it impossible to verify compliance without parsing AC1's intricate conditions, violating the checklist requirement for unambiguous stateful contracts.

findings.title: Inconsistent handling of 'unclear' adjudication outcomes
findings.body: The Evidence tier section defines 'unclear' as 'not terminal' and states it blocks counting (line 1074), while the Decision-gate consistency matrix row for 'Evidence-tier transition' repeats this but adds 'an adjudication whose every compared finding carries the `unclear` outcome is not terminal' (line 1324). However, the Business Rules section (line 1172) states the same rule but uses slightly different phrasing: 'an `unclear` outcome is not terminal, because the dependency contract defines it as needing more human review before it can be used as quality evidence'. These are functionally equivalent but create unnecessary redundancy and potential for subtle interpretation drift. Consolidating this into one authoritative definition would improve clarity.

findings.title: Redundant repetition of 'real-pull-request' in objective O11
findings.body: The Brief Objective List states 'O11: Do not measure real-pull-request effect until the minimum number of dogfooded pull requests fixed in AC15 (ten, with adjudicated evidence) have accumulated.' The term 'real-pull-request' is unnecessarily repeated here when 'dogfooded pull requests' already implies the same context (Ronda's own repository reviews). Simplifying to 'O11: Do not measure effect until the minimum number of dogfooded pull requests...have accumulated' would improve readability without losing meaning.

findings.title: Contradictory definition of 'terminal adjudication' for evidence tier transitions
findings.body: The 'Evidence tier' section defines 'terminal adjudication' as requiring every compared finding to carry one of several outcomes including 'ronda_miss', 'ronda_better', 'duplicate', or a 'Ronda-only outcome' or 'Ronda finding rejected' outcome, or confirming a clean result. However, the 'Decision-gate consistency matrix' row for 'Evidence-tier transition' repeats this definition but omits 'ronda_better' from the list of terminal outcomes (line 1173), while the 'Business Rules' section (line 742) and the 'Evidence tier' table description (line 1009) explicitly include 'ronda_better' as terminal. This contradiction creates ambiguity about whether a pull request with only 'ronda_better' outcomes qualifies for the 'real_pr_measured' tier.

findings.title: Inconsistent handling of 'unclear' outcome in evidence tier transitions
findings.body: The 'Evidence tier' section states that an 'unclear' outcome is 'not terminal' and therefore prevents a pull request from counting toward the 'real_pr_measured' tier (line 1015). However, the 'Decision-gate consistency matrix' row for 'Evidence-tier transition' contradicts this by listing 'unclear' as a terminal outcome in its example text (line 1197): 'An adjudication whose every compared finding carries the `unclear` outcome is not terminal — the dependency contract defines `unclear` as needing more human review before it can be used as quality evidence — so that pull request does not count'. The example text incorrectly implies 'unclear' is terminal by stating it 'is not terminal', which is a double negative that misstates the rule. This creates confusion about the status of 'unclear' outcomes in the tier transition logic.

findings.title: Contradictory 'Claim admissibility' requirements for 'unclear' outcomes
findings.body: The 'Claim admissibility' gate in the 'Decision-gate consistency matrix' states that a real-pull-request claim is 'not admissible' if 'the cohort must be closed and terminally adjudicated first, because leaving unfavorable cases unresolved while adjudicating favorable ones is cohort selection, not evidence' and defines 'terminal' as requiring outcomes including 'ronda_miss', 'ronda_better', 'duplicate', or 'Ronda-only outcome' or 'Ronda finding rejected' (line 1252). However, the same gate's description later states 'a counted cohort of ten pull requests whose compared findings all carry the `unclear` outcome is inadmissible: `unclear` is not a terminal outcome, so those pull requests are not adjudicated and the count is zero' (line 1280). These two statements conflict: the first implies 'unclear' is not terminal and thus blocks admissibility, while the second correctly identifies 'unclear' as non-terminal but then misattributes the inadmissibility to the count being zero rather than to the cohort not being closed and terminally adjudicated, which is the primary gate condition. This undermines the gate's logical consistency.

findings.title: Ambiguous scope of 'sweep-enabled review' definition
findings.body: The 'Business Rules' section defines 'sweep-enabled review' as 'a review whose pass actually ran the sweep and reported a category list version as used' (line 1077). However, the 'Decision-gate consistency matrix' row for 'Sweep enablement resolution' states that an 'unrecognized' enablement value results in a non-sweep review (line 1125), and the 'Business Rules' section clarifies that such a pass 'records that the enablement value was unrecognized' (line 725). This creates ambiguity: does a pass that records an unrecognized value but otherwise runs the review logic qualify as 'sweep-enabled' under the line 1077 definition, or does the 'reported category list version' requirement exclude it? The definition should clarify whether 'reporting a version' is strictly required or if other sweep metadata suffices.

findings.title: Redundant repetition of 'terminal adjudication' definition
findings.body: The definition of 'terminal adjudication' is repeated verbatim in three locations: the 'Evidence tier' table description (line 1007), the 'Decision-gate consistency matrix' row for 'Evidence-tier transition' (line 1173), and the 'Claim admissibility' gate description (line 1252). This redundancy increases maintenance burden and risk of inconsistency. The spec should define this term once in a dedicated 'Definitions' section and reference it elsewhere.

findings.title: Contradictory sweep enablement behavior
findings.body: The spec states in 'Use Case 1' (line 120) that an unrecognized non-empty enablement value means the sweep runs as a 'non-sweep review', but the 'Sweep enablement resolution' matrix (line 1413) states the unrecognized case is an 'Off' outcome that produces the 'same non-sweep review as the absent case'. These conflict: one says the sweep runs (but as non-sweep), the other says it is Off and does not run. The matrix is the normative source per its header, so the Use Case text must be corrected to state the sweep is Off and does not run.

findings.title: Missing evidence tier transition for list revision at 'fixture_only'
findings.body: The 'Valid transitions' table (line 147) states 'fixture_only' remains unchanged on a list revision, but the AC15(b) text (line 2028) says 'a revision cannot leave `fixture_only`, since the tier is driven by whether any sweep-enabled real-PR review is recorded, which a revision does not undo'. This creates ambiguity: if a revision occurs while at 'fixture_only' and no sweep-enabled review has been recorded, the tier must remain 'fixture_only', but the table's phrasing 'unchanged — a revision cannot leave `fixture_only`' is redundant and potentially misleading. The table should explicitly state the tier remains 'fixture_only' when no sweep-enabled review exists, aligning with AC15(b)'s logic.

findings.title: Overly complex description of 'unclear' outcome exclusion
findings.body: The AC15(b) text (line 2028) defines 'unclear' as non-terminal due to needing more human review, but the explanation is buried in a dense paragraph with nested clauses. This reduces clarity for operators who need to understand why 'unclear' blocks the ten-pull-request count. It should be simplified to a direct statement: 'An adjudication with an `unclear` outcome is not terminal because the dependency contract requires further human review before it can be used as quality evidence, so pull requests with only `unclear` outcomes do not count toward the ten.'

findings.title: Inconsistent terminology for 'unrecognized' enablement value
findings.body: The 'Sweep enablement resolution' matrix (line 1413) uses 'non-empty and unrecognized' while the 'Use Case 1' text (line 120) says 'non-empty value that is not recognized'. Consistency in terminology ('unrecognized') across all sections improves readability and reduces ambiguity.

findings.title: Contradictory definition of 'terminal adjudication' for clean results
findings.body: The 'Evidence tier' section defines a terminal adjudication for a clean result as requiring confirmation by 'the recorded same-head external review' (line 1217), but the 'Claim admissibility' matrix (line 1722) and AC15(b) (line 1558) state that a clean result is terminal only when 'the clean result `clean_agreement` is confirmed', without mentioning the external review as a prerequisite. This creates ambiguity about whether an external review is mandatory for a clean result to count toward the ten-pull-request threshold. The definitions must align: either the external review is required for all clean results, or the 'Evidence tier' section's additional condition is an error.

findings.title: Inconsistent 'terminal adjudication' requirement for clean results
findings.body: The 'Claim admissibility' matrix (line 1722) states that a clean result (`clean_agreement`) is terminal, while the 'Evidence tier' section (line 1217) adds the condition that it must be 'confirmed by the recorded same-head external review'. AC15(b) (line 1558) echoes the matrix's simpler definition. This contradiction means the spec does not unambiguously define when a clean result counts toward the ten-pull-request threshold. The spec must pick one definition and apply it consistently across all sections that reference terminal adjudication.

findings.title: Missing specification of how 'unclear' outcomes are resolved to terminal status
findings.body: The spec repeatedly states that an `unclear` outcome is 'not terminal' and requires 'more human review' (e.g., lines 1472, 1562, 1725), but it never defines the process or criteria for resolving an `unclear` outcome into a terminal one (e.g., `ronda_miss`, `duplicate`, etc.). Without this, the ten-pull-request count cannot be completed, as `unclear`-only pull requests would permanently block progression to `real_pr_measured`. The spec should describe the adjudication workflow for `unclear` cases.

findings.title: Ambiguous scope of 'matched sweep-off control' for comparative claims
findings.body: The 'Claim admissibility' matrix (line 1745) and AC15(d) (line 1588) require a 'matched sweep-off control on the same pull request heads' for comparative claims, but the spec never defines what constitutes a 'matched' control. Does it require identical model credentials, exact same configuration (beyond sweep setting), or identical timing? This ambiguity makes it impossible to determine if evidence satisfies the requirement. The spec should explicitly list the attributes that must match between sweep-on and sweep-off runs.

findings.title: Redundant repetition of 'Ronda-only outcome' definition
findings.body: The phrase 'a Ronda-only outcome (the outcome recorded for a valid defect the external reviewer did not find, which AC15(d) defines)' appears verbatim in multiple locations (e.g., lines 1658, 1725, 1749). While consistent, this repetition increases maintenance burden and risks inconsistency if the definition changes. The spec should define this term once in a dedicated glossary or definitions section and reference it elsewhere.

findings.title: Contradictory definition of 'terminal adjudication' for evidence tier transition
findings.body: The 'Evidence tier' section defines a terminal adjudication as requiring every compared finding to carry one of several outcomes including 'ronda_miss', 'ronda_better', 'duplicate', or a 'Ronda-only outcome' or 'Ronda finding rejected' outcome, or confirming a clean result. However, the 'Decision-gate consistency matrix' row for 'Evidence-tier transition' repeats this definition but omits 'ronda_better' from the list of terminal outcomes in its description (line 1179), while the table cell for 'Valid transitions' correctly includes it (line 1140). This omission creates a direct contradiction between two normative sections defining the same gate condition, making the transition rule ambiguous and untestable.

findings.title: Missing URL-serialized state definition for category list version
findings.body: The spec introduces the concept of a 'category list version' (e.g., AC3, AC7, AC19) that is used in review summaries, logs, and evidence tracking, and states it must be a 'non-blank scalar string' (AC19). However, it never explicitly defines the allowed key names, format, or allowed values for this version when serialized in URLs (e.g., in links to the recorded list artifact, API endpoints for list retrieval, or webhook payloads referencing the version). Per the review checklist, URL-serialized state introduced without explicit parameter key names and allowed values forces implementers to guess the serialization contract.

findings.body: Step 2 of Use Case 1 states 'Ronda considers the changed content against every category... This is what a pass that completes review execution does', but the postconditions later state 'A pass that completes review execution satisfies this in full'. However, AC1 explicitly defines 'reaching review execution' as reading changed files and running the review, not completing it. The spec's repeated use of 'completes review execution' (lines 141, 152, 161) contradicts AC1's definition and creates ambiguity about whether the guarantee applies only to passes that finish all review logic or also to those that fail after file reading but before finalization.

findings.title: Per-category pass record surface assignment lacks specification for benchmark runs
findings.body: The 'Operational Visibility' section states the per-category pass record appears in 'the benchmark output and its logs' for benchmark runs, but AC1 (line 541) only specifies surfaces for 'real-PR pass superseded before publication' and 'completed benchmark run' without naming 'benchmark output' as a surface. AC1 says 'the record on the logs, together with whatever per-category output that pass's own surface carries (the benchmark output for a benchmark run)', but fails to explicitly assign 'benchmark output' as a required surface in the AC1 text itself, creating a gap between the business rule and the acceptance criterion.

findings.title: Contradictory failure shape definitions for 'credential-pattern-gap' category
findings.body: The 'credential-pattern-gap' category's failure shape in the table (line 1194) states 'A qualified, camelCase, hyphenated, prefixed, or wrapped credential the guard's pattern does not match', but the AC13 definition of 'harder' credential patterns (line 1527) lists exactly these same variants (qualifier/prefix, camelCase, hyphenated, wrapping) as the exhaustive set that makes a case 'harder'. This creates a contradiction: the category's failure shape implies these variants are defects (i.e., the guard fails to match them), while AC13 treats them as intentional test cases. The failure shape must be revised to describe the actual defect (e.g., 'A guard pattern that matches only the canonical form but misses its qualified, camelCase, hyphenated, prefixed, or wrapped variants') to align with AC13's test logic and avoid requiring guards to match non-canonical forms.

AC13 then mandates adding a 'harder credential-pattern case' to the fixture, directly seeding one of the very kinds the business rules forbid using as a list basis. This creates a logical inconsistency: the spec both prohibits seeding unconfirmed kinds and requires seeding one of them. The business rule must be revised to clarify that while the list cannot be *based on* unconfirmed kinds, the fixture may still *include* them for measurement purposes, or AC13 must be reworded to reference only real-PR-confirmed variants.

findings.body: The plan states in 'Layer-by-Layer Changes' (line 429) that `parseBooleanFlag` alone cannot recognize `default` as off. This is a technical accuracy claim about framework behavior that must be verified against the actual source file (`src/config/load-config.ts`). Since the plan does not cite the authoritative source line number or provide evidence from the codebase confirming this limitation, it is unverified and must be confirmed by the implementer before proceeding.

findings.title: Missing verification for `sweepModeRaw` field usage
findings.body: The plan states in 'Layer-by-Layer Changes' (line 489) that `sweepModeRaw` is carried but never rendered, and that unit tests assert its absence from output surfaces. However, the 'Testing Strategy' section (line 501) only lists scenarios for enablement resolution and list validation, with no explicit test scenario for verifying `sweepModeRaw` is never logged or published. This leaves a gap in coverage for a critical security requirement (preventing raw value leakage), so the test plan must add this scenario.

findings.title: Add missing Document Quality Gate log
findings.body: The PR description is absent, so the required current Document Quality Gate log is missing. Because the spec contains stateful constructs (evidence tier transitions, category-list currency, and regression-gate status), the log should also include a Matrix coherence preflight row or a reasoned Not applicable.

findings.title: Add decision-gate consistency matrix
findings.body: The spec introduces decision-gate behavior for evidence tier promotion/demotion, category-list currency, seeded-benchmark regression-gate restoration, and default-enablement evidence gates. The supplied Coverage Matrix only maps objectives to acceptance criteria. The checklist requires a decision-gate consistency matrix or pointer identifying gate inputs, allowed outcomes, required next actions, mirror surfaces, and examples where applicable.

findings.title: Resolve no-current-category-list state
findings.body: Business Rules say exactly one sweep category list is current at any time, and Use Case 1 requires a current list. Statuses / Enum Values and AC6 say the recorded list cannot be marked current while Open Questions 1 and 8 leave candidates undecided. The spec does not define what happens if sweep is enabled before a current list exists, nor reconcile the exactly-one-current rule with this interim state.

findings.title: Define testable enablement values for AC18
findings.body: AC18 defers the concrete configuration key and refers to recognized on/off values without naming them or referencing an existing parsing contract. Without the key or allowed values, implementers and tests cannot determine whether a supplied value enables, disables, or is unrecognized.

findings.title: Require same fixture version in AC8 recall comparison
findings.body: Use Case 3 and Business Rules require sweep-on and sweep-off comparison runs to use the same fixture version, but AC8 only requires the same target, model, and configuration and merely reports fixture version. Add the same-fixture-version condition to AC8 so the recall/variance evidence is admissible as written.

findings.title: Specify cost aggregation for repeated passes
findings.body: Use Case 4 and AC11 require model calls and elapsed time per pass for both configurations, but the benchmark/precision evidence may involve multiple runs. The spec does not say whether to record per-run values, min/mean/max, or another summary, making cost comparison non-reproducible.

findings.title: Settle operator-facing surface for per-category pass record
findings.body: AC1 and AC20 require the per-category pass record to be visible to an operator, but Operational Visibility and Open Question 7 leave the surface undefined. Without a named surface or a minimum testable contract, these acceptance criteria cannot be verified and implementation must guess.

findings.title: Clarify whether Open Questions 2 and 3 block default enablement
findings.body: The Open Questions table says questions 2 and 3 block making the sweep the default, while the Business Rules say recall/variance/cost results do not pass or fail a default-enablement gate unless thresholds are later set. Clarify whether answering questions 2 and 3 is a prerequisite for the default-enablement decision or merely optional evidence.

findings.title: Clarify historical tier relabeling on list revision
findings.body: AC15(c) requires evidence previously labeled Real-PR evidence (measured) to be relabeled provisional when the category list changes. If quality evidence artifacts are immutable historical records, this conflicts with traceability. Clarify whether the tier labels claims under the current list or whether historical records retain their original tier.

findings.title: Clarify regression-gate restoration action
findings.body: AC17 says the regression gate is restored once AC12 and AC13 cases exist, while Use Case 5 says the operator declares the extended fixture usable. State whether restoration is automatic upon fixture changes or requires an operator decision/record.

findings.title: Align non-sweep review wording with unrecognized-value recording
findings.body: Use Case 1 defines non-sweep review as the review published with sweep off, but unrecognized enablement values still produce a non-sweep review while recording that the value was unrecognized. AC18 describes disabled behavior as if the feature were absent. Clarify which records are produced for absent, disabled, unrecognized, and missing-list cases.

findings.title: Clarify display-label usage in review summaries
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values says category display labels are read in review summaries, but AC3 and Operational Visibility only require the review summary to state that the sweep was active and the list version. If category labels are not shown in summaries, remove or qualify that statement.

findings.title: Add Document Quality Gate log to PR description
findings.body: The PR description is absent, so there is no current Document Quality Gate log. The checklist treats a missing log as important by default. Add a current log, and because the spec contains stateful evidence-tier transitions, include the Matrix coherence preflight row or a reasoned Not applicable.

findings.title: Add consistency matrix for evidence-tier and category-list gates
findings.body: The spec adds decision-gate state: Evidence tier transitions, category-list currency, and default-enablement evidence gates. The existing Coverage Matrix does not identify gate inputs, allowed outcomes, required next actions, mirror surfaces, or examples. Add the required consistency matrix or pointer before ready-for-human-review.

findings.title: Define behavior when sweep is enabled and category list is not current
findings.body: Use Case 1 requires a current list, Business Rules say exactly one list is current, and Statuses says the recorded list cannot be current while Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved. AC19 only handles unreadable, empty, or malformed lists. Define what an enabled sweep does when a readable list is not marked current, including the initial no-current-list state.

findings.title: Resolve conflict over whether counted real PRs must be sweep-enabled
findings.body: Business Rules and Evidence tier transitions speak of pull requests reviewed under the current list, while Use Case 6 and AC15(b) require the counted pull requests to be sweep-enabled. These are not equivalent if a review can occur with the sweep disabled or unrecognized. State the counting rule consistently.

findings.title: Clarify evidence tier after list revision restarts count
findings.body: Valid transitions keep a revised measured record at provisional and keep a revised provisional record provisional, while AC15(b) says a record with no sweep-enabled real pull request review recorded is fixture_only. After a revision restarts the count at zero, it is unclear whether the tier is provisional or fixture_only. Clarify whether recorded means under the current list version and define the post-revision tier.

findings.title: Fix AC10 conflict with uncategorized findings
findings.body: AC10 says a pass that finds nothing for every swept category publishes a clean result. Use Case 1 and AC20 require uncategorized findings to be published. If an uncategorized finding exists, the pass found nothing for swept categories but must not publish a clean result. Reword AC10 to cover total findings or explicitly allow uncategorized findings.

findings.title: Specify operator-facing surface for per-category pass record
findings.body: AC1, AC19, and AC20 require records on an operator-facing surface, but Open Question 7 leaves that surface unset. As written, the criteria cannot be tested or implemented. Choose a surface or define a minimum required surface in the spec.

findings.title: Clarify AC14 secret prohibition for synthetic fixture values
findings.body: AC14 prohibits credential values, tokens, and authorization values in quality evidence, while AC13 and Use Case 5 require planted credential-pattern fixture cases. Clarify that the prohibition applies to real secrets, or define how synthetic fixture values are permitted.

findings.title: Define adjudicated external-finding evidence
findings.body: AC15 and Use Case 6 make adjudicated external-finding evidence a gate for measured real-PR evidence, but the spec does not define adjudication or point to the criteria in the depended-on spec. Add a definition or an explicit pointer so the gate is testable.

findings.title: Define unexpected finding for precision fixtures
findings.body: Use Case 4 and AC9 count unexpected findings and clean fixtures but do not define what a fixture expects. Define unexpected finding relative to fixture expectations, including whether precision fixtures may expect findings and how those are counted.

findings.title: State baseline sample count for 2026-09-10 recall baseline
findings.body: AC8 requires the sample count to be at least as large as the 2026-09-10 baseline's, but the spec does not state that baseline sample count or identify where it is recorded. Without that value, compliance cannot be checked.

findings.title: Identify recorded per-pull-request convergence figures for cost comparison
findings.body: AC11 and the Business Rules require comparison against recorded per-pull-request convergence figures, but the spec does not identify the artifact, location, or values. Cite the exact cost baseline record.

findings.title: Specify recognized enable/disable values for sweep configuration
findings.body: AC18 says empty or unrecognized enablement values are off, but it does not define the configuration key or the recognized on and off values. Specify the canonical key and values, or a pointer, so unrecognized-value behavior can be tested.

findings.title: Define how matched sweep-off control coexists with one-review-per-head
findings.body: Use Case 6 requires a matched sweep-off control on the same pull request heads, recorded but not published. Business Rules and AC2 require one review per head SHA and no second published review. Define how an unpublished control pass is produced and recorded without violating the one-review contract.

findings.title: Reconcile gate restoration for seeded benchmark
findings.body: AC17 says the regression gate is restored once AC12 and AC13 cases exist, while Use Case 5 also requires re-running the benchmark and an operator declaration. State the complete gate-restoration criteria.

findings.title: Resolve Open Question 9 conflict with mandatory matched control
findings.body: Business Rules and Use Case 6 state that comparative claims require a matched sweep-off control, while Open Question 9 asks whether that control is required. Clarify whether the matched-control rule is normative now or only a placeholder pending decision.

findings.title: Reconcile candidate accounting rule with awaiting candidates
findings.body: Statuses says every candidate is either swept or excluded, then lists candidates awaiting a human decision that are neither. Qualify the rule to current recorded lists or move the awaiting candidates into an explicit pending state.

findings.title: Add explicit triggers to use cases
findings.body: The use cases provide actors, preconditions, steps, and outcomes, but most do not name an explicit trigger. Add trigger statements for each use case.

findings.title: Reconcile plural harder credential variants with AC13
findings.body: Use Case 5 says the operator adds harder credential-pattern variants, while AC13 requires at least one harder case. Align the requirement and acceptance criterion.

findings.title: Distinguish the two different four-item sets
findings.body: The spec uses four for both the seeded benchmark never-found kinds and the unseeded real-PR themes. Name the sets explicitly wherever they are referenced to avoid confusion.

findings.title: Require run timestamps in AC8
findings.body: Use Case 3 and Operational Visibility include run timestamps, but AC8 does not require timestamps in the committed evidence. Add timestamps to AC8 or remove them from the required evidence.

findings.title: Track deferral D1 human confirmation
findings.body: Deferral Note D1 requests human confirmation that rebalancing remains out of scope, but no open question or awaiting-decision row tracks it. Add it to the decision list or state that it is not blocking.

findings.title: Correct open question blocking references
findings.body: The Open Questions table says questions 1 and 8 block AC4, but AC4 only requires metadata for categories that are already on the list. Those questions block AC6 and list currency, not AC4. Correct the mapping.

findings.title: Specify variance metric
findings.body: The objective is run-to-run variance, but AC8 only requires lowest, highest, and sample count. State whether min/max range is the intended variance metric or specify the variance measure.

findings.title: Add missing Document Quality Gate log
findings.body: The PR description is empty, but the checklist requires a current Document Quality Gate log for spec PRs. Add the log to the PR description; because the spec contains stateful evidence-tier transitions, include a Matrix coherence preflight row or a reasoned not-applicable note.

findings.title: Add decision-gate consistency matrix
findings.body: The spec introduces decision gates (evidence-tier claim admissibility, category-list currency in AC6, regression-gate restoration in AC17, and enablement/list fallback in AC18/AC19) but provides only an objective coverage matrix. Add a consistency matrix or pointer that identifies each gate's inputs, allowed outcomes, required next actions, mirror surfaces, and examples where relevant.

findings.title: Define recognized sweep enable/disable values
findings.body: AC18 requires off for empty or unrecognized values but does not define the configuration key's recognized on/off values. Without the allowed value set, implementers must guess the serialization contract and AC18 cannot be tested. Specify the canonical accepted values or explicitly defer them with a testable rule.

findings.title: Define enabled-sweep behavior when no current category list exists
findings.body: AC6 says the recorded list cannot be marked current while Open Questions 1 and 8 are unresolved, while AC18 allows the sweep to be enabled and Use Case 1 assumes a current list. AC19 only covers unreadable, empty, or malformed lists, not a missing or non-current list. State the fallback behavior for an enabled sweep with no current list.

findings.title: Specify the per-category pass record surface
findings.body: AC1 and AC20 require the per-category pass record to be visible on an operator-facing evidence surface, but Operational Visibility and Open Question 7 leave the surface undecided. As written, the criteria cannot be tested. Choose a surface or define a minimum testable surface before approval.

findings.title: Make AC10 clean-pass criterion unambiguous
findings.body: AC10 says a pass that finds nothing for every swept category publishes a clean result, but the spec also allows uncategorized findings. Clarify whether AC10 applies only when there are no published findings at all, or how uncategorized findings affect a clean result.

findings.title: Make AC11 cost comparison testable
findings.body: AC11 requires comparing model calls and elapsed time per pass against recorded per-pull-request convergence figures, while Use Case 4 says the cost baseline contains no Ronda pass cost. Define what evidence, format, or threshold constitutes the required comparison, or reword AC11 to require contextual reporting only.

findings.title: State the baseline sample count in AC8
findings.body: AC8 refers to the 2026-09-10 baseline sample count without naming it. The Overview mentions five runs; state the minimum sample count or the exact baseline artifact in AC8 to avoid relying on external context.

findings.title: Align wording that counted PRs are sweep-enabled
findings.body: Use Case 6 and the Business Rules speak of pull requests reviewed under the current category list version, while Considerations and AC15 require sweep-enabled reviews. Use consistent language that only sweep-enabled reviews count toward the real-PR tier.

findings.title: Clarify regression-gate restoration action
findings.body: AC17 says the gate is restored once AC12 and AC13 cases exist, but Use Case 5 requires an operator declaration that the extended fixture is usable. Clarify whether existence alone restores the gate or whether a recorded operator declaration is required.

findings.title: Add current Document Quality Gate log with Matrix coherence preflight
findings.body: The PR description is missing, so there is no current Document Quality Gate log. The spec adds stateful decision-gate behavior (Decision-gate consistency matrix, evidence-tier transitions, AC15 claim-admissibility gates), so the log must also carry a Matrix coherence preflight row or a reasoned Not applicable. Add the log before approval.

findings.title: Define an objective category-membership test for AC15(d)
findings.body: AC15(d) makes the real-PR denominator depend on defects being 'within the sweep's claim' by an objective match against swept categories and failure shapes, but it also says the per-category pass record does not decide membership and provides no operational rule for determining a match. It further requires two adjudicators to derive the same membership from textual categories and failure shapes. As written, membership is not testable and the pass-record/adjudication roles conflict. Make the pass record authoritative for pass-published findings or define deterministic matching rules and required adjudication fields.

findings.title: Resolve AC1 ambiguity for failures after a finding result exists but before publication
findings.body: Use Case 1 says 'not determined' is recorded only when a pass fails before its review result exists. AC1 includes publication-call failures before the review is public but does not say whether the per-category values are 'not determined' or ordinary produced-findings/produced-none when the model result already exists. This leaves a required record ambiguous. State explicitly what a pass records when failure occurs after the finding result is established but before publication.

findings.title: Define behavior for supersession before review execution
findings.body: AC1 treats a pass superseded before publication as a completed pass whose record is on the logs, while AC2 says supersede behavior is unchanged. The spec does not say what happens if supersession ends the pass before review execution. Since AC1 says pre-review skips emit no sweep metadata, clarify whether a superseded-before-execution pass emits no sweep metadata or some other record.

findings.title: Define the record when review execution fails before any review request is issued
findings.body: AC1 defines reached categories as those carried by an issued review request and says a pass that fails before issuing any request has reached none. Use Case 1 and AC1 also say every pass that reaches review execution records per-category outcomes. It is unclear whether such a pass emits an empty per-category record, no per-category record, or other sweep metadata. Define the required output for this case.

findings.title: Terminal miss record does not cover recorded sweep-off control misses
findings.body: The Terminal miss record section requires only sweep_enabled_miss and external_review_miss when all compared reviewers report no findings but human adjudication records a defect. If a sweep-off control is recorded, it is also a compared reviewer and its miss affects comparative recall, but no code value or rule records the control miss. Add a control-miss entry or state precisely how the control miss is derived and recorded.

findings.title: Define adjudication when both Ronda configurations report the same defect
findings.body: The adjudication outcomes define ronda_only for a valid defect reported by the sweep-enabled review or a recorded control and not by the external reviewer, and duplicate for a valid defect both reviewers found. They do not define how to adjudicate the same defect reported by both the sweep-enabled review and the sweep-off control when the external reviewer did not report it, or whether both findings receive terminal outcomes. This affects numerator attribution and terminal adjudication. Define the outcome(s) and counting rule.

findings.title: No terminal record is defined for human-only defects outside the sweep claim
findings.body: AC15(b) says a clean result requires human adjudication to record no defect, while terminal miss records apply only to defects within the sweep's claim. If human adjudication records a real defect outside the sweep's claim and no compared reviewer reported anything, the head is neither clean nor terminally missed and has no compared finding outcome. This can leave an eligible pull request permanently unadjudicated. Define a terminal head-level record or state that such defects are ignored for adjudication.

findings.title: AC18 defers exact enablement key and recognized values
findings.body: AC18 makes enablement behavior depend on the existing durability-mode switch vocabulary but defers the concrete key name and exact on/off values to planning. As written, testers and implementers must look outside the spec to know the accepted values. Enumerate the recognized values or cite the exact existing contract that defines them.

findings.title: Cohort cutoff wording conflicts between Use Case 6 and AC15(b)
findings.body: Use Case 6 defines the eligible cohort as pull requests whose pass completed by the recorded cutoff. AC15(b) and the business rule define it as pull requests that carried a sweep-enabled review up to the cutoff. Completion and carrying a review may diverge, for example when a pass starts before the cutoff but publishes after it. State which event or timestamp governs cohort membership.

findings.title: Baseline comparability requirement is ambiguous when baseline reproduction is impossible
findings.body: AC8 requires a repeated original-fixture comparison for baseline comparability, but also says the 2026-09-10 baseline cannot support baseline reproduction and that no field of the new run is compared against the recorded alias. It is unclear what comparability the repeated original-fixture runs establish or how they relate to the 2026-09-10 baseline. Clarify the metric being established or rename the requirement.

findings.title: Repeated real-PR recall and cost comparisons lack an anti-selection rule
findings.body: AC15(d) fixes run sets and requires all attempted runs for variance claims, and it fixes the matched control run set, but for comparative recall or cost claims where configurations are run more than once it does not require every attempted run to enter evidence or the run set to be fixed before results are observed. This permits selecting favorable repetitions for recall or cost comparisons. Extend the run-set fixation and all-attempts rule to all repeated comparative real-PR evidence.

findings.title: Benchmark evidence does not forbid dropping attempted runs
findings.body: AC8 and AC11 require recorded benchmark runs to be paired and have equal length, but they do not state that every attempted benchmark run under the compared configurations enters the evidence. This allows omitting unfavorable or failed runs while keeping the remaining sequences paired. Require all attempted runs to be recorded or define explicit non-outcome-aware exclusion criteria.

findings.title: AC1 does not explicitly assign surfaces for the unrecognized-enablement record
findings.body: AC18 and Operational Visibility say the unrecognized-enablement record is carried on the surfaces AC1 assigns, but AC1 itself assigns surfaces for the per-category record and does not explicitly mention the unrecognized-enablement record. Add an explicit surface assignment or cross-reference in AC1.

findings.title: Fix 'only two tests are gating' wording
findings.body: The business rule says only two tests are gating for default enablement, then lists that recall, variance, precision, and cost evidence must all have been recorded and that precision must not have regressed. Reword this as two conditions or enumerate the gating requirements consistently.

findings.title: Name excluded seeded never-found kinds individually in the list section
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values excludes 'the seeded benchmark's four never-found kinds' as a group, while only the Overview names the four kinds. For a complete recorded category list, enumerate each excluded candidate in the list section itself.

findings.title: Define run ordering for AC11 run-position pairing
findings.body: AC11 pairs benchmark cost observations by run position within each configuration's identical run sequence, but does not say how run order is established or recorded. Timestamps are required by AC8, but the pairing rule should state whether position is chronological, recorded sequence order, or another deterministic ordering.

findings.title: Define where clean_agreement is recorded for heads with no compared findings
findings.body: AC15(b) counts a clean result only when confirmed by clean_agreement, but the adjudication-outcome table applies to compared findings and the terminal miss record applies only when a defect exists. The spec does not define the head-level clean_agreement record for a pull request with no compared findings. Define the record location and required fields.

findings.title: Add missing Document Quality Gate log
findings.body: The PR description is absent and therefore contains no current Document Quality Gate log. The spec adds stateful constructs such as evidence-tier transitions and a decision-gate consistency matrix, so the log should also carry a Matrix coherence preflight row or a reasoned Not applicable. Add the current log before approval.

findings.title: Define 'sweep pass' and exclude degraded passes from per-category guarantees
findings.body: Use Case 1 Postconditions says every sweep pass that reaches review execution records per-category results, but Use Case 1 Considerations, AC18, and AC19 require enabled passes with unrecognized enablement or unreadable, empty, or malformed lists to run ordinary non-sweep reviews and record only sweep-did-not-run or unrecognized-enablement metadata. The spec defines 'sweep-enabled review' but not 'sweep pass', so it is unclear whether degraded enabled passes are sweep passes. Define the term and make the per-category postcondition apply only to passes that actually run the sweep.

findings.title: Reconcile AC1 surface assignment for published passes whose check-run write fails
findings.body: AC1 first says a pass that completes review execution and publishes a review has the per-category record on both check-run output and logs. Later it says that when the review is already public but a success check-run write fails after bounded retry, the record is on the logs only, with whatever surface the write produced. The decision-gate matrix repeats the conditional rule. Remove the absolute statement or make it explicitly conditional on the pass's own write producing a check run whose outcome is a review.

findings.title: Define an objective category-membership test for AC15(d)
findings.body: AC15(d) and Use Case 6 make confirmed-defect membership depend on an objective match against swept categories and failure shapes, while saying recorded entries are not decisive. No testable rule explains how a defect is matched to a category or how disagreement is resolved. Without this, the recall denominator and claim admissibility cannot be tested. Specify the membership test or make adjudication outcomes the authoritative recorded decision with explicit rules.

findings.title: Require adjudications to record the swept category for non-pass findings
findings.body: AC15(d) says membership for external-reviewer findings and human-only defects is decided by the adjudication naming the swept category. No acceptance criterion, adjudication outcome enum, or operational surface requires an adjudication to carry a category field. Add that recording requirement or cite the existing contract that provides it.

findings.title: Clarify whether unpublished or terminally failed sweep-enabled passes count in AC15(b)
findings.body: Use Case 6 and AC15(b) count pull requests that carried a sweep-enabled review or whose pass completed by a cutoff, but the business rule defines a sweep-enabled review as a pass that ran the sweep and reported a list version, not necessarily one that published a review. AC1 also recognizes superseded passes and terminal failures after review execution. State whether unpublished or failed passes can be sweep-enabled reviews for the ten-pull-request count and how clean or miss adjudication works when no Ronda findings were published.

findings.title: Extend terminal miss record to cover recorded sweep-off controls
findings.body: The Terminal miss record section defines only `sweep_enabled_miss` and `external_review_miss` and requires both together. If a sweep-off control is recorded and all compared reviewers report no findings while human adjudication records an in-claim defect, the control's miss has no terminal record, even though AC15(d)'s comparative recall denominator includes human-recorded defects and control results. Add a control miss code or rule that the terminal miss record covers every recorded configuration.

findings.title: Assign explicit surfaces for sweep-did-not-run and unrecognized-enablement records
findings.body: AC18 and AC19 say these records are made on the surfaces AC1 assigns, but AC1's surface assignment is written for per-category records and does not describe degraded non-sweep passes that have no per-category record. Operational Visibility says same surfaces, but AC1 itself leaves the assignment ambiguous. Specify the surfaces for these records directly or amend AC1 to cover them.

findings.title: Define what baseline comparability requires in AC8
findings.body: AC8 says baseline comparability for the original-thirteen subset requires a repeated original-fixture comparison, then says the 2026-09-10 baseline lacks the fields for baseline reproduction and that no field of the new run is compared against the recorded alias. It never states what evidence or metric makes the new comparison comparable. Define the comparability requirement or replace the term with the exact records to produce.

findings.title: Fix contradictory precision-pairing dimensions in AC15(d) and the matrix
findings.body: AC15(d) says paired precision evidence is not paired on reviewed target, fixture version, or sample count, but then says the fixture target and the sweep arm are the only dimensions the pairing leaves out. The Decision-gate consistency matrix similarly says identical apart from fixture target and sweep arm. Reconcile the excluded dimensions so implementers know whether fixture version and sample count are excluded.

findings.title: Resolve AC15(d)'s contradiction about unreported attempted runs
findings.body: AC15(d) says every attempted run under the configurations enters the evidence, then says an attempt run but not reported does not exist for the clause. These cannot both be true. State that unreported attempts make the evidence inadmissible or must be recorded as missing attempts, rather than saying they do not exist.

findings.title: Scope AC6 to the initial list or allow revisions
findings.body: AC6 says the swept list holds exactly the five categories in Statuses / Enum Values, while Use Case 2 and the Business Rules allow later list revisions that add, remove, or reorder categories. As written, AC6 would fail after any approved revision. Scope it to the initial recorded version or rewrite it as a requirement about the initial list and candidate accounting.

findings.title: Record run position for AC11's paired cost metric
findings.body: AC11 pairs benchmark cost runs by run position, but AC8 only requires timestamps, sample count, and per-run recall. If run order is not recorded, pairing by position is ambiguous. Require an explicit run index or define position deterministically from timestamps.

findings.title: Clarify defect-weighted recall
findings.body: Use Case 3 and AC15(d) use defect-weighted recall but define it as confirmed defects reported divided by confirmed defects, with no weights. Use defect-level recall or define the weighting scheme.

findings.title: Enumerate recognized sweep enablement values or cite the existing vocabulary
findings.body: AC18 defers the exact on and off values to the plan and only says they match the existing durability-mode switch. For a testable operator contract, enumerate the allowed values in the spec or reference the exact existing definition.

findings.title: State where a clean result is published
findings.body: AC10 requires a pass that finds nothing to publish a clean result, but does not say whether that appears in the review body, summary, check run, or logs. Tie the clean result to the existing non-sweep clean-review surface.

findings.title: Update `ronda_rejected` description for both-reviewer findings
findings.body: The `ronda_rejected` table description says it applies to a finding reported by the sweep-enabled review or control, but the following paragraph says it also applies when both the external reviewer and Ronda raised the finding. Add that case to the table description to avoid a two-meaning reading.

findings.title: Specify precedence between environment and workflow input
findings.body: AC18 says environment or workflow input outranks the operator config file but does not say which of environment and workflow input wins when both supply non-empty values. If existing precedence already defines this, cite it; otherwise specify the ranking.

findings.title: Add missing Document Quality Gate log
findings.body: The PR description is empty, but the checklist requires a current Document Quality Gate log in the PR description. This spec also contains stateful constructs (Evidence tier transitions and the Decision-gate consistency matrix), so the log should include a Matrix coherence preflight row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable. Add the current log before approval.

findings.title: Define unpublished matched controls and repeated real-PR runs
findings.body: AC15(d) and Use Case 6 require matched sweep-off controls, and repeated variance runs, on the same real pull-request heads while saying those runs are recorded but not published. AC2 and the Business Rules still require exactly one review per head SHA and publication whenever the existing flow reaches publication. The spec does not define an offline/control pass type, a publication suppression path, or how repeated real-PR runs avoid creating second reviews. Define the execution and record surfaces for these non-publishing runs, or remove the comparative claims that depend on them.

findings.title: Resolve contradictory membership rule for sweep claim
findings.body: AC15(d) and Use Case 6 say membership for a pass-published finding is determined by its per-category pass record, but then say no recorded entry decides membership and that an objective match test decides instead. The objective test is not defined beyond saying a defect either matches a category or does not, despite categories being textual failure shapes. This makes the confirmed-defect denominator and recall measurement untestable. Name one authoritative membership rule and define the objective matching procedure.

findings.title: Add category-membership fields to adjudication records
findings.body: AC15(d) requires adjudications for external findings and human-only defects to name the swept category matched by the defect.
