The Adjudication outcomes and Terminal miss record tables only define code values, display labels, and descriptions; they define no category-membership field or record shape. Add the required adjudication field or point to the existing record contract that carries it.

findings.title: Extend terminal adjudication to head-level miss records and human-only defects
findings.body: AC15(b) and Use Case 6 define terminal adjudication as every compared finding carrying a terminal outcome or a clean result being confirmed. They also rely on terminal miss records and on defects recorded only by human adjudication. The spec does not say how a head becomes terminal when a human-only defect exists, especially when other compared findings are present, nor does the terminality definition include head-level terminal miss records. Update the terminal-adjudication rule to cover these cases explicitly.

findings.title: Include recorded sweep-off controls in terminal miss record
findings.body: The real-PR business rule makes a recorded sweep-off control a compared reviewer, but the Terminal miss record only defines sweep_enabled_miss and external_review_miss. If all compared reviewers report no findings and human adjudication records a defect, a recorded control would also have missed that defect, yet the spec provides no control miss entry or terminality rule. Add a control miss record or state how this case is terminally adjudicated.

findings.title: Define treatment of out-of-scope human-recorded defects on clean heads
findings.body: A clean result requires human adjudication to record no defect, while AC15(d) excludes defects outside the sweep claim from the measurement universe. If human adjudication records a real defect that is outside the sweep claim on an otherwise clean head, the spec does not say whether the clean result is blocked, whether the head is terminal, or how the count is affected. Clarify how out-of-scope human-recorded defects interact with clean results and terminality.

findings.title: Make precision regression test detect new noise on already-noisy fixtures
findings.body: Use Case 4 declares precision regression only when sweep-on unexpected findings exceed sweep-off totals or when a fixture clean in every sweep-off run becomes not clean. If a fixture is already not clean under sweep-off, sweep-on can introduce different unexpected findings with no total increase and no clean-to-not-clean transition, hiding a regression. Require per-fixture or per-finding comparison, or require precision fixtures to be clean in the sweep-off arm.

findings.title: Require per-run found and missed seeded defect identities in AC8
findings.body: Use Case 3 says information shown includes per-run found and missed seeded defects, but AC8 only requires per-run recall and per-defect found/missed counts across runs. Without per-run defect identities, the reported recall evidence cannot be independently checked against the spread requirement. Add a requirement that each run records which seeded defects were found and missed.

findings.title: Clarify baseline comparability versus baseline reproduction
findings.body: AC8, the Business Rules, and the Coverage Matrix require a repeated original-fixture comparison for baseline comparability, but AC8 also says no run against the 2026-09-10 baseline is classified as baseline reproduction and no field is compared against the recorded alias. It is unclear what evidence establishes comparability or how it is tested. Define the required comparability evidence or reword to avoid implying a baseline comparison that the spec forbids.

findings.title: Fix precision-pairing dimension contradiction
findings.body: AC15(d) says paired precision evidence need not match the reviewed target, fixture version, or sample count, but later says the fixture target and sweep arm are the only dimensions the pairing leaves out. The Decision-gate matrix example also allows target, fixture version, and sample count differences. Reconcile these statements and enumerate the allowed mismatching dimensions exactly once.

findings.title: Make cohort cutoff objectively testable
findings.body: AC15(b) and Use Case 6 require the eligible cohort to be closed by a recorded cutoff fixed in advance before any eligible pass findings are visible. The spec does not define what visible means, what timestamp or event constitutes the cutoff, or where the cutoff is recorded. Specify an observable cutoff rule, such as pass start or publication timestamp and the evidence surface that records it.

findings.title: Define sweep pass consistently
findings.body: AC3, AC20, and Operational Visibility use the term sweep pass, while enabled-but-degraded passes are described as ordinary non-sweep reviews. Without a definition, AC20 could be read to apply to degraded passes that have no per-category record. Define sweep pass explicitly, preferably as a pass that actually ran the sweep, and state that degraded passes are excluded.

findings.title: Clarify whether unpublished terminal-failure passes are sweep-enabled reviews
findings.body: The Business Rules define a sweep-enabled review as a review whose pass ran the sweep and reported a category list version. AC1 and Operational Visibility can record the list version for a terminal failure after review execution even when no review is published. Evidence-tier promotion depends on the first sweep-enabled real-PR review being recorded. State whether such unpublished terminal-failure passes count as sweep-enabled reviews for tier transitions and counts.

findings.title: Define record for terminal failures that reach review execution but issue no review request
findings.body: AC1 says reached categories are those carried by the review request and that a failure before issuing any request reaches none. It does not say what a pass that reached review execution but issued no request must emit: an empty per-category record, a record stating zero categories reached, or no record. Define the required log/check-run content for this edge case.

findings.title: Specify initial category list version and activation date
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values defines the initial category list but does not provide a list version, revision-history entry, or current-version activation date. AC7 and AC19 require a non-blank version, revision history, and activation date for the recorded list. Add the initial version and date, or state where and how they are assigned as part of making the list current.

findings.title: Clarify check-run surface for public failures after review execution
findings.body: AC1 says that when a failure occurs after the review is public, the per-category record is on the logs in either case, with whatever per-category surface the check-run write produced. The governing rule says check-run output carries the record only when the pass's own check-run write produced a check run whose outcome is a review. State explicitly whether a landed success check run also carries the record.

findings.title: Define effect of recording a sweep-off control with no findings
findings.body: AC15(c) says a recorded control can demote measured evidence because the control's findings become compared findings. If the recorded control has no findings, it is unclear whether the head remains counted, whether adjudication is reopened, or whether demotion can occur. State the no-findings control rule explicitly.

findings.title: Use stable mirror references in decision-gate matrix
findings.body: The Decision-gate consistency matrix cites mirror surfaces with approximate line numbers such as ~106, ~120, and ~541. These will stale quickly. Replace them with stable section, Business Rule, or AC references.

findings.title: Correct pass record before review phrasing
findings.body: AC15(d) and Use Case 6 refer to the pass record before review. The per-category pass record is written during or after review execution, not before review. Rephrase to at review time or before adjudication.

findings.title: Clarify only two tests are gating wording
findings.body: The Business Rules say only two tests are gating for default enablement, then list that all evidence must be recorded and precision must not regress. These are conditions, not tests. Rephrase to avoid confusion.

findings.title: Enumerate excluded never-found kinds in the list section
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values excludes the seeded benchmark's four never-found kinds but does not name them there. Use Case 2 names them. For traceability of the recorded list, enumerate the four excluded kinds in the category-list section.

findings.title: Clarify attempted-run reporting wording
findings.body: AC15(d) says every attempted run enters the evidence, but also says an attempt run but not reported does not exist for the clause. Rephrase to say that all attempted runs must be reported and that unreported attempts are inadmissible.

findings.title: Add missing Document Quality Gate log to PR description
findings.body: The PR description is absent, so there is no current Document Quality Gate log. The review checklist treats a missing log as an important finding by default. Add a current Document Quality Gate log to the PR description.

findings.title: Add Matrix coherence preflight row for stateful contracts
findings.body: The spec contains stateful constructs, including Evidence tier transitions and the Decision-gate consistency matrix. The Document Quality Gate log must therefore carry a Matrix coherence preflight row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable. Add that row to the PR description.

findings.title: Define terminal adjudication for human-only defects when the head is not all-clean
findings.body: AC15(d) includes defects recorded only by human adjudication in the confirmed-defect denominator, but AC15(b), Use Case 6, and the Terminal miss record section only provide a terminal miss record for heads whose compared reviewers all reported no findings. If a head has other compared findings and human adjudication adds a defect none of them reported, there is no compared-finding outcome and no terminal miss record, so the pull request cannot become terminally adjudicated or counted. Define a head-level terminal record or outcome for this case.

findings.title: Define handling of human-only defects outside the sweep claim on otherwise clean heads
findings.body: AC15(b) makes a clean result require human adjudication to have recorded no defect, while the Terminal miss record only covers defects within the sweep claim. An outside-claim human-recorded defect on an otherwise clean head therefore blocks clean confirmation but has no terminal path. State whether outside-claim human defects block the count and, if so, how they are terminally recorded.

findings.title: Include recorded sweep-off control in terminal miss record
findings.body: The Terminal miss record section requires only sweep_enabled_miss and external_review_miss, but a recorded sweep-off control is also a compared reviewer. If all compared reviewers reported no findings and human adjudication records a defect within the sweep claim, the control miss is not terminally recorded. Add a control-miss code value or an explicit rule covering this case.

findings.title: Clarify adjudication when both Ronda and external raised a rejected or out-of-scope finding
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values says ronda_better applies only to external-only findings, then says ronda_rejected applies including when both Ronda and the external reviewer raised a rejected or out-of-scope finding. The ronda_rejected description only covers Ronda-reported findings, leaving the external finding's terminal outcome unclear. Define the outcome for jointly raised rejected or out-of-scope findings.

findings.title: Make category-membership rule testable and reconcile it with pass records
findings.body: AC15(d) makes category membership an objective match but also says per-category pass records do not decide membership and that a misrecording carries no membership, without defining how an objective match is verified or corrected. This is not testable as written. Define the authoritative matching evidence and the correction process.

findings.title: Resolve ambiguous meaning of reached for terminal failures
findings.body: Use Case 1 describes a terminal failure as considering only the categories it reached, while AC1 defines reached as categories carried in the issued review request, even if the pass failed before any consideration occurred. This can record categories as reached or not determined when no review consideration happened. Reconcile the term or use separate terms.

findings.title: Specify operator-facing enablement key and allowed values
findings.body: AC18 defers the concrete configuration key name and exact on/off values to planning, but the acceptance criterion requires an operator to enable and disable the sweep. Without the key and allowed values, the operator-facing contract cannot be tested. Enumerate them or state the existing durability-mode vocabulary explicitly.

findings.title: Address assumption that historical model remains available
findings.body: AC8 requires repeated original-fixture runs with the historical model and configuration held constant. This assumes the historical model remains available; if it is not, baseline comparability is impossible. State the fallback or exception.

findings.title: Require precision evidence to use the same category-list version as the paired recall claim
findings.body: AC9 requires precision runs to record the category-list version but does not require that version to match the recall comparison being claimed, while AC15(d) and the business rules require paired precision evidence on the same category-list version. Add the matching requirement to AC9.

findings.title: Reconcile late single-head sweep-off controls with closed-cohort control rules
findings.body: Evidence tier transitions and AC15(c) allow a sweep-off control recorded on a head inside a measured cohort to demote the tier, but AC15(d) requires a matched control to cover the whole closed cohort and have its run set fixed in advance. Clarify whether such late single-head controls are only tier-affecting and never admissible for comparative claims, and how they interact with the closed cohort.

findings.title: Clarify contradictory language about attempted runs in variance evidence
findings.body: AC15(d) says every attempted run under the configurations enters the evidence, but then says an attempt run but not reported does not exist for the variance clause. These statements conflict. State whether unreported attempts are invalid, must be recorded, or are ignored.

findings.title: Fix pass record before review ordering in AC15(d)
findings.body: AC15(d) says the pass record exists before review, but AC1 and AC20 place the per-category pass record at review time or after findings exist. Correct the ordering to at review time before adjudication.

findings.title: Remove trailing sentence fragment in decision-gate matrix example
findings.body: The Decision-gate consistency matrix's Claim admissibility example ends with a stray sentence fragment 'they do not pair the claim.' after the rerun-control example. Remove the fragment.

findings.title: Fix duplicated used in AC9
findings.body: AC9 contains the duplicated word 'used. used.' Remove the duplicate.

findings.title: Clarify precedence between environment and workflow input
findings.body: AC18 lists environment or workflow input above the operator config file but does not state which of environment and workflow input has precedence when both supply non-empty values. Clarify or reference the existing precedence rule.

findings.title: Align AC12 theme name with category display label
findings.body: AC12 says 'record identity', while the category display label is 'Record identity and deduplication'. Use the exact category name for consistency.

findings.title: Avoid implementation detail bounded retry in AC1
findings.body: AC1 references a 'bounded retry', which is an implementation detail. Replace it with the observable outcome or refer generically to the existing check-run recovery behavior.

findings.title: Define clean result for AC10
findings.body: AC10 uses 'clean result' without defining whether it means a review with no findings or an existing clean-review artifact. Define the term or reference the existing contract.

findings.title: Clarify pass completed cutoff in Use Case 6
findings.body: Use Case 6 and AC15(b) close the cohort using pull requests whose pass completed by a cutoff. It is unclear whether completed means review execution, publication, or a successful review. Define the completion event.

findings.title: Correct mirror surface reference for sweep enablement matrix row
findings.body: The Sweep enablement resolution matrix row cites Use Case 1 step 1, but the enablement rule appears in Use Case 1 preconditions and considerations. Cite the correct mirror surface.

findings.title: Define outcome for external-only real defects outside the sweep claim
findings.body: AC15(d) excludes ronda_better as an external-only finding considered noisy or irrelevant. It does not say which outcome applies to an external-only real defect that is outside the sweep claim. Define the outcome and its denominator treatment.

findings.title: Clarify duplicate outcome with multiple Ronda configurations
findings.body: AC15(d) describes duplicate as a valid defect both reviewers found, but with sweep-enabled review, sweep-off control, and external reviewer it is unclear which pair triggers duplicate. Define duplicate for multi-configuration comparisons.

findings.title: Clarify AC9 precision requirements when multiple precision fixtures exist
findings.body: AC9 requires the same target, fixture version, and sample count for precision runs, while Use Case 4 allows at least one precision fixture. If multiple precision fixtures exist, the required target and sample count are ambiguous. Define how multiple fixtures are handled.

findings.title: Add current Document Quality Gate log with Matrix coherence preflight
findings.body: The PR description is absent, so the required current Document Quality Gate log is missing. Because the spec adds stateful contracts (decision-gate matrix, evidence-tier transitions, precedence rules), the log must include a Matrix coherence preflight row or a reasoned Not applicable. Add the log before approval.

findings.title: Scope AC6 to the initial list or make it revision-aware
findings.body: AC6 says the current swept list holds exactly the five initial categories and the named excluded entries. Use Case 2, Business Rules, and AC7 allow later list revisions that add or remove categories. As written, any revised current list would fail AC6. Scope AC6 to the initial list version or restate it as a per-version candidate-accounting requirement.

findings.title: Define terminal miss recording for a recorded sweep-off control
findings.body: AC15(b) and the Terminal miss record section require only sweep_enabled_miss and external_review_miss when all compared reviewers report no findings but human adjudication records a defect. A recorded sweep-off control is also a compared reviewer, but its miss has no terminal record. Add a control miss code or define how the control miss is terminally recorded so comparative recall and cost can be computed.

findings.title: Define count handling for human-recorded out-of-scope defects with no compared finding
findings.body: AC15(b) makes a clean result require human adjudication recorded no defect, and terminal miss records only defects within the sweep claim. If human adjudication records an out-of-scope defect and no compared finding exists, the pull request is neither clean nor terminally adjudicated. Define this case, for example by treating out-of-scope human-only defects as non-blocking for the count or by adding a terminal out-of-scope record.

findings.title: Define per-category record for publication failures after the finding result exists
findings.body: AC1 distinguishes not-determined failures before the review result exists from ordinary values after the review is public, but it does not state what a pass records when the finding result exists and publication then fails. Clarify that such a pass records produced-findings or produced-none, not not determined.

findings.title: Define review result used by AC1
findings.body: AC1 relies on whether the review result exists, but the spec never defines review result. Define it as the final findings payload or another concrete artifact so the not-determined boundary is testable.

findings.title: Define check run whose outcome is a review
findings.body: AC1 and the decision matrix condition surface assignment on a check run whose outcome is a review, but that phrase is not defined. Define it or cite the existing contract that defines it.

findings.title: Clarify existing-check automatic skip
findings.body: AC1 and Use Case 1 refer to an existing-check automatic skip as a pre-review skip, but AC2 only names draft-skip and supersede behavior. Define the existing-check skip or align AC1 and AC2.

findings.title: Clarify AC10 applies only to sweep-enabled passes and define clean result
findings.body: AC10 does not say it applies only to sweep-enabled passes and does not define clean result. It could be read to require clean-result publication for non-sweep passes. State that it governs sweep-enabled passes reaching publication and define clean result as a review with zero findings.

findings.title: Specify enablement key and allowed values or reference them explicitly
findings.body: AC18 defers the concrete operator-configuration key name and exact on/off values to planning, while making enablement an acceptance criterion. Either specify the key and allowed values in the spec or reference the existing durability-mode contract precisely enough to test.

findings.title: Define precedence between environment and workflow input
findings.body: AC18 says environment or workflow input outranks the operator config file but does not say which of environment and workflow input wins when both supply non-empty values. Define the full precedence order.

findings.title: Make category membership matching testable
findings.body: AC15(d) says membership is an objective match against category failure shapes and that a misrecorded pass entry carries no membership, but it provides no testable procedure or criteria. Define how membership is objectively decided and corrected, or make the adjudication record authoritative.

findings.title: Add standard deviation to Use Case 3 information shown
findings.body: Use Case 3 postconditions and AC8 require the population standard deviation of per-run recall, but Use Case 3 Information shown omits it. Add the standard deviation to the information shown.

findings.title: Add paired cost differences to Use Case 4 information shown
findings.body: AC11 and Use Case 4 postconditions require comparative cost to be stated as paired per-run differences, but Use Case 4 Information shown lists only standalone model calls and elapsed time. Add the paired differences to the information shown.

findings.title: Provide traceable evidence-source rows for initial categories
findings.body: The Statuses preamble says the evidence source names the corpus rows behind each category, but most table entries only name the corpus. Add row identifiers or citations for each category and excluded candidate to make the evidence traceable as AC4 and Use Case 2 require.

findings.title: Define wrapped in another construct for harder credential cases
findings.body: AC13 lists wrapped in another construct as an exhaustive hardness condition but does not define what qualifies as wrapping. Provide examples or a testable definition.

findings.title: Define pass completed in Use Case 6 cohort closure
findings.body: Use Case 6 says the cohort contains pull requests whose pass completed by the cutoff, but does not say whether completed means review execution, publication, or terminal adjudication. Define the completion point.

findings.title: Provide initial category list version and revision history
findings.body: The initial category list section says the list can be marked current but does not state a non-blank scalar version, activation date, or initial revision entry. AC19 treats a missing list version as malformed, and AC7 requires version and revision history. Add the initial version and revision record or state that the recording process creates them.

findings.title: Remove duplicated word in AC9
findings.body: AC9 contains a duplicated sentence fragment: used. used. Remove the duplicate.

findings.title: Remove stray sentence in Claim admissibility example
findings.body: The Claim admissibility example in the Decision-gate consistency matrix ends with a stray sentence, they do not pair the claim., after the control-rerun example. Remove or relocate it.

findings.title: Replace approximate line-number pointers in matrix mirror surfaces
findings.body: The Decision-gate consistency matrix uses approximate line-number pointers such as ~106, ~120, and ~541. Replace them with stable section or AC references.

findings.title: Clarify only two tests are gating wording
findings.body: The business rule says only two tests are gating for default enablement but then describes multiple evidence conditions. Reword to identify the two gating conditions clearly.

findings.title: Use shared denominator wording in AC15(d)
findings.body: AC15(d) says a configuration's denominator is zero, but the denominator is the shared confirmed-defect universe for the head set. Reword to avoid implying per-configuration denominators.

findings.title: Fix phrasing in Use Case 2 information shown
findings.body: Use Case 2 Information shown says the sub-themes named as below the candidate boundary. Rephrase to named as being below the candidate boundary or similar.

findings.title: Add missing Document Quality Gate log with Matrix coherence preflight
findings.body: The PR description is empty, so the required current Document Quality Gate log is missing. Because the spec adds stateful contracts (evidence-tier transitions, adjudication outcomes, terminal miss records) and decision gates, the log should include the Matrix coherence preflight row or a reasoned Not applicable. Add the log to the PR description.

findings.title: Define objective, testable membership test for swept claim
findings.body: AC15(d) makes swept-claim membership depend on an 'objective match' and a 'closing test' but never defines a testable matching rule beyond saying a defect matches a category or failure shape. It also says the per-category pass record does not decide membership while relying on that record as the place where membership appears. Define the objective matching rule, including ambiguous and multiple-category cases, and state the required record fields.

findings.title: Handle recorded sweep-off control in terminal miss record
findings.body: Use Case 6, AC15(b), and Terminal miss record require a terminal miss record when all compared reviewers report no findings but human adjudication records a defect. A recorded sweep-off control can be a compared reviewer, but only `sweep_enabled_miss` and `external_review_miss` are defined. Add a control miss record or state how the control is terminally adjudicated and how its miss enters recall.

findings.title: Define handling for human-recorded defects outside the swept claim on all-clean heads
findings.body: AC15(b) handles all-clean heads with no human-recorded defect and with a human-recorded defect within the swept claim, but not with a human-recorded defect outside the swept claim. State whether such a head is clean/counted or how it is terminally adjudicated, because as written it may never count even though the defect is outside the measurement.

findings.title: Make duplicate and Ronda-only counting conditional on swept-claim membership
findings.body: AC15(d) says `duplicate` and Ronda-only outcomes count as confirmed defects, while earlier it says uncategorized or outside-claim defects are not confirmed defects. Clarify that these outcomes count only when the underlying defect is within the swept claim, otherwise the rules conflict.

findings.title: Fix zero-denominator rule to cover non-clean external reviews with excluded outcomes
findings.body: AC15(d) describes a zero denominator as implying that external reviews' clean results are confirmed. Zero confirmed defects can still occur when external findings exist but are adjudicated `ronda_better` or `ronda_rejected`. Rewrite the zero-denominator rule to depend only on absence of confirmed defects within the swept claim.

findings.title: Define published clean result required by AC10
findings.body: AC10 requires publication of a 'clean result' but no section defines what that publication contains or where it appears. Define the clean result, for example as a review with no findings plus the required summary, so AC10 is testable.

findings.title: Define unexpected finding for precision fixtures
findings.body: Use Case 4 and AC9 count unexpected findings for precision fixtures but only require at least one fixture that expects a clean result. Define unexpected finding relative to a fixture's expected result, especially for any fixture that does not expect a completely clean review.

findings.title: Specify configuration key and allowed on/off values in AC18
findings.body: AC18 defers the concrete configuration key and exact on/off values to planning, while making the enablement contract testable only through those values. Enumerate the accepted on/off values or cite the exact existing durability-mode contract, and state the key or the authoritative reference.

findings.title: Replace internal review-request definition of reached categories with observable product rule
findings.body: AC1 defines reached categories by whether an internal review request carried them. This is an implementation detail and may not be observable from product evidence. Define reached in observable product terms or require a recorded surface that shows which categories were included before the failure.

findings.title: Specify record field for adjudication-named swept category
findings.body: AC15(d) requires adjudications for non-pass findings and human-recorded defects to name the swept category, but the adjudication outcome enum only defines code values. Specify the record field or surface that carries the named category so membership decisions can be recorded and audited.

findings.title: Include standard deviation in Use Case 3 information shown
findings.body: Use Case 3 postconditions and AC8 require the standard deviation of per-run recall, but the Information shown list omits it. Add the standard deviation to Use Case 3 information shown.

findings.title: Include paired cost differences in Use Case 4 information shown
findings.body: Use Case 4 postconditions and AC11 require paired per-run cost differences, but Information shown only lists standalone model calls and elapsed time. Add the paired differences to the information shown.

findings.title: Remove duplicated 'used.' in AC9
findings.body: AC9 contains duplicated text: 'used. used.' Remove the duplicate.

findings.title: Remove stray sentence in claim admissibility example
findings.body: The Claim admissibility matrix example ends with a stray fragment 'they do not pair the claim.' after the control-rerun example. Remove or correct the sentence.

findings.title: Correct 'pass record before review' wording in AC15(d)
findings.body: AC15(d) says membership decisions are recorded 'the pass record before review', but the pass record is written during or after review execution and before adjudication. Reword to avoid saying before review.

findings.title: Clarify default-enablement gating wording
findings.body: Business Rules says only two tests are gating and then lists recall, variance, precision, and cost evidence plus no precision regression. Reword to identify the two gating conditions: all required evidence recorded, and no precision regression.

findings.title: Distinguish sweep-did-not-run and unrecognized-enablement records
findings.body: Operational Visibility describes a sweep-did-not-run record that also covers unrecognized enablement values, while AC18 and the decision-gate matrix treat the unrecognized-enablement record as separate from sweep-did-not-run. Distinguish the records or use one consistent name.

findings.title: Enumerate the four never-found kinds in excluded candidates
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values and AC6 refer to the seeded benchmark's four never-found kinds as excluded candidates without enumerating them there. Enumerate the four kinds in the excluded-candidates record for completeness.

findings.title: State precedence between environment and workflow input
findings.body: AC18 gives precedence as environment or workflow input over operator config file but does not say which of environment and workflow input wins when both supply non-empty values. State the precedence or cite the existing operator-configuration rule.

findings.title: Add the Document Quality Gate log to the PR description
findings.body: The PR description is missing the required Document Quality Gate log. Because the spec adds stateful decision gates and an evidence-tier lifecycle, the log also needs a Matrix coherence preflight row or a reasoned Not applicable entry.

findings.title: Remove the contradiction about where adjudication code values are fixed
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values says it is the only site that fixes ronda_only and ronda_rejected and that no other site restates them, but AC15(d) explicitly restates both code values. Remove the values from AC15(d) or change the sole-site rule so the sections agree.

findings.title: Define an objective category-membership test for real-PR defects
findings.body: AC15(d) makes claim membership depend on an objective category match and says recorded entries can be misrecordings, but it never defines a testable matching rule. As written, two implementers could compute different denominators. Define concrete membership rules or make a named adjudication field authoritative.

findings.title: Specify the enablement key and recognized on/off values
findings.body: AC18 makes recognized on/off values and the configuration key planning decisions, but enablement outcomes depend on whether a value is recognized. Enumerate the accepted values and key in the spec or cite the exact existing contract that defines them.

findings.title: Resolve precedence between environment and workflow input
findings.body: AC18 says environment or workflow input outranks the config file, but does not say which of environment and workflow input wins when both supply non-empty different values. Specify the full precedence order.

findings.title: Define a check run whose outcome is a review
findings.body: AC1 and the pass-outcome matrix assign records based on a check run whose outcome is a review, but the spec never defines that condition. Define the exact check-run state or conclusion that satisfies it.

findings.title: Define when the review result exists
findings.body: AC1 distinguishes failures before the review result exists from failures after the review is public, but does not define when the review result exists. This determines whether reached categories are recorded as not determined or as produced findings or none.

findings.title: Define the existing-check automatic skip referenced by AC1
findings.body: AC1, AC19, and the business rules rely on an existing-check automatic skip and cite AC2, but AC2 only names draft-skip and supersede. Define the existing-check skip or correct the references.

findings.title: Require adjudications to name swept categories for claim membership
findings.body: AC15(d) says membership for external findings and human-only defects is recorded by adjudication naming the swept category, but no acceptance criterion requires adjudications to include a category or defines what happens when one is missing. Add that requirement and a fallback.

findings.title: Include recorded sweep-off controls in terminal miss records
findings.body: When all compared reviewers are clean but human adjudication records a defect, AC15(b) and Use Case 6 require a confirmed miss for the sweep-enabled review and external reviewer only. If a sweep-off control is recorded, its miss status is undefined. Include all compared Ronda configurations or state that no control may exist.

findings.title: Make the cohort cutoff verifiable
findings.body: The cohort must be closed before findings or results are visible, but visibility is not defined and no audit evidence is required. Define what visible means and how the cutoff is proven, for example a timestamp before review publication.

findings.title: Scope AC10 to sweep-enabled passes that ran the sweep
findings.body: AC10 can be read to apply to any pass, including non-sweep or degraded passes where there are no swept categories. Scope it to a sweep-enabled pass that actually ran the sweep and reaches publication.

findings.title: Clarify precision evidence target for real-PR recall claims
findings.body: AC15(d) requires AC9 precision evidence for real-PR recall claims on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count, while AC9 describes fixture runs. Clarify whether the target is the precision fixture set and how it is paired with the real-PR heads.

findings.title: State whether precision regression blocks recall claims
findings.body: AC15(d) requires a recorded precision regression result for a recall claim but does not say whether a regressed result makes the claim inadmissible, while the later default-enablement gate requires no precision regression. State the claim-admissibility effect of a precision regression.

findings.title: Define run-position pairing and per-head run completeness for cost metrics
findings.body: AC11 pairs benchmark runs by run position and AC15(d) reduces repeated real-PR runs per head, but neither defines run ordering, failed or missing runs, or whether every head must have the same run count. Specify these rules to make cost metrics testable.

findings.title: Condition duplicate outcomes on sweep-claim membership
findings.body: AC15(d) says the denominator contains only defects within the sweep claim, but it also says a duplicate outcome counts once without conditioning it on claim membership. Clarify that duplicate defects outside the swept claim are excluded.

findings.title: Define the recording surface and execution path for unpublished sweep-off controls
findings.body: AC15(d) and Use Case 6 require matched sweep-off controls on real PR heads, recorded but not published, while the one-review-per-head contract remains. The spec does not say how such controls are executed, where their findings and cost are recorded, or how skips are avoided. Define the control path and record surfaces.

findings.title: Handle multiple human-recorded defects in clean-review adjudication
findings.body: AC15(b) and Use Case 6 describe the human-recorded defect behind clean reviewers in the singular. State that every human-recorded defect must receive a terminal miss record when more than one exists.

findings.title: Define sweep pass consistently
findings.body: The spec uses sweep pass both for passes enabled to sweep and for passes that actually executed the sweep. AC3 and AC20 depend on this distinction. Add a definition and use it consistently.

findings.title: Handle equal variance results
findings.body: AC15(d) requires a variance comparison as a direction, higher or lower, but does not cover equal standard deviations. State the equal or no-direction outcome.

findings.title: Clarify the two gating tests for default enablement
findings.body: The business rule says only two tests are gating for default enablement, then lists recall, variance, precision, and cost evidence plus precision non-regression. Rephrase to identify the two gating tests.

findings.title: Align log visibility with degraded cases
findings.body: Operational Visibility says logs record that the sweep ran and the list version, but AC18 and AC19 have degraded or unrecognized cases with no list version. Qualify the log statement to cases where the sweep actually ran.

findings.title: Add missing Document Quality Gate log
findings.body: The PR description is absent, so there is no current Document Quality Gate log. This spec also contains stateful decision gates and evidence-tier transitions, so the log should include a Matrix coherence preflight row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable. Add the log to the PR description.

findings.title: Fix impossible precision-evidence requirement for real-PR recall claims
findings.body: AC15(d) says a comparative real-PR recall claim requires the paired precision evidence AC9 defines on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count. AC9 is fixture-based, while a real-PR comparison has no fixture version and its target is a cohort of pull request heads. As written, the recall-claim admissibility rule cannot be satisfied. Separate benchmark precision evidence from real-PR recall evidence or rewrite the requirement in terms that apply to real-PR cohorts.

findings.title: Resolve contradictory sweep-claim membership rule
findings.body: AC15(d) says membership for a pass's own published finding is determined by its per-category pass record entry, but then says no recorded entry decides membership and that a run entry contradicting the objective match is a misrecording carrying no membership. This makes the authoritative source of membership unclear and leaves misrecorded categories unresolved. State exactly which artifact is normative, how an objective match is evaluated, and how misrecordings are corrected.

findings.title: Define required category attribution in adjudication records
findings.body: AC15(d) requires membership for external-reviewer findings and human-recorded defects to be established by adjudication naming the swept category. The adjudication outcome definitions and terminal-outcome lists do not require or define a category field. Without that field, the confirmed-defect denominator cannot be recorded or tested. Add an explicit requirement that adjudication evidence records the swept category or uncategorized status for every defect used in the claim.

findings.title: Define per-category outcome for failure after result exists but before publication
findings.body: AC1 defines not determined only for failures before the review result exists and ordinary produced-findings/produced-none values for failures after the review is public. It does not define the record for a failure after the result exists but before publication, such as a publication-call failure after the result is generated. State which per-category values that case records.

findings.title: Specify enablement key and recognized on/off values
findings.body: AC18 defers the concrete configuration key name and exact recognized on/off values to planning. That leaves the operator enablement contract untestable as written because an implementer or tester cannot know what configuration surface or vocabulary is valid. Either state the key and allowed values, or reference an existing documented switch precisely enough to test.

findings.title: Define unpublished sweep-off control run mechanism
findings.body: AC15(d) and Use Case 6 require matched sweep-off control reviews on the same real-PR heads, recorded but not published. The spec does not define how such control passes are executed, recorded, or kept compatible with the one-review-per-head SHA contract. Define the control-pass lifecycle, record surfaces, and how it avoids publishing a second review.

findings.title: Clarify ronda_better semantics for out-of-scope external findings
findings.body: The spec uses ronda_better both as the dependency contract's outcome for an external-only finding adjudicated noisy or irrelevant and as the external-origin equivalent for findings rejected or out of scope of the sweep claim. Those are different concepts: a valid real defect outside the sweep claim is not necessarily noisy or irrelevant. Clarify the meaning or introduce a distinct outcome, because this affects the denominator.

findings.title: Clarify duplicate outcomes outside sweep claim
findings.body: AC15(d) says a duplicate outcome is a valid defect both reviewers found and counts once, while the denominator is limited to defects within the sweep's claim. It is unclear whether a duplicate finding that matches no swept category is counted or excluded. State how duplicate outcomes interact with swept-category membership.

findings.title: Define treatment of adjudicated defects outside sweep claim for counted PRs
findings.body: AC15(b) says a clean result requires human adjudication to record no defect, but it does not say what happens when adjudication records a real defect that is outside the sweep's claim. It is unclear whether that pull request is clean, counted, or which terminal outcome applies. Define this case explicitly.

findings.title: Define 'check run whose outcome is a review'
findings.body: AC1 and the decision-gate matrix assign records based on whether the pass's own check-run write produced a check run whose outcome is a review. The phrase is never defined. Without a definition, the surface assignment is ambiguous. Define the term or replace it with observable product-level conditions.

findings.title: Clarify review-execution boundary for file-read and request-composition failures
findings.body: AC1 says reaching review execution means the pass reads changed files and runs the review, but it does not say how to classify failures while reading changed files, composing the review request, or after reading but before issuing a request. These cases determine whether categories are reached and what is logged. Define the boundary precisely.

findings.title: Make cohort cutoff and closure evidence verifiable
findings.body: AC15(b) and Use Case 6 require the eligible cohort to be closed before adjudication and before any eligible pass's findings are visible, with a recorded cutoff fixed in advance. The spec does not define what recorded evidence proves the cutoff was fixed before findings were visible or that the cohort was closed. Define the required timestamps or artifacts.

findings.title: Remove ambiguity about sweep-off-only reviews in counted evidence
findings.body: AC15(b) refers to findings from either Ronda configuration as compared findings, while the counted-pull-request rule requires the pull request to have carried a sweep-enabled review. This can be read as allowing a sweep-off-only review to count. Clarify that sweep-off evidence is compared only when a sweep-enabled review exists for that head.

findings.title: Define an objective membership test for swept-category claims
findings.body: AC15(d) claims two adjudicators will derive the same membership because a defect either matches a recorded category or does not, but it provides no testable matching rule for descriptions and failure shapes. Define the objective criteria or make the recorded adjudication category authoritative.

findings.title: Correct 'pass record before review' wording
findings.body: AC15(d) says membership is recorded with the pass record before review, but the per-category pass record is produced by the review pass, not before it. The intended meaning appears to be before adjudication or before the claim is read. Correct the wording.

findings.title: Reconcile sole-site outcome code value claim with AC15 restatement
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values says it is the only site that fixes the ronda_only and ronda_rejected code values and that no other site restates them, but AC15(d) later restates those code values. Either remove the restatement or relax the sole-site claim.

findings.title: Replace approximate line-number mirror pointers with stable references
findings.body: The decision-gate consistency matrix uses approximate line-number pointers such as ~106, ~120, and ~541. These are unstable and can drift. Use stable section names, AC numbers, or headings instead.

findings.title: Reduce implementation detail in reached-category rule
findings.body: AC1 defines reached categories in terms of the internal review request the pass issued and assumes the sweep composes one request from the recorded list. This over-prescribes implementation and may be hard to test from product behavior. Define reached categories in observable terms, such as categories included in the pass's recorded review attempt.

findings.title: Add standard deviation to Use Case 3 information shown
findings.body: Use Case 3 postconditions and AC8 require the standard deviation of per-run recall, but the Information shown list for Use Case 3 omits it. Add the standard deviation to that list for consistency.

findings.title: Define non-sensitive counts
findings.body: Operational Visibility says logs record non-sensitive counts but does not say which counts are included or what makes them non-sensitive. Define the allowed log contents or reference the existing logging rule.

findings.title: Add the Document Quality Gate log
findings.body: The PR description is absent, so the required current Document Quality Gate log is missing. Because the spec contains stateful contracts (evidence tiers, adjudication outcomes, decision gates), the log also needs the Matrix coherence preflight row. Add the complete log to the PR description.

findings.title: Fix real-PR precision evidence requirement
findings.body: AC15(d) requires a comparative real-PR recall claim to carry the paired precision evidence AC9 defines on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count as the claimed heads. AC9 and Use Case 4 define fixture-based precision runs that expect clean results; real pull-request heads are not fixtures, have no fixture version, and may contain real defects. The requirement cannot be satisfied or tested as written. Define real-PR precision evidence or remove the fixture-specific pairing from AC15(d).

findings.title: Reconcile empty enablement value handling
findings.body: Use Case 1 says an absent, empty, or whitespace-only enablement value means off and counts as not supplied. AC18 and the Sweep enablement resolution matrix row say an empty value at a higher-precedence source defers to the next source, which can make the effective value On. Clarify that the off outcome applies only after precedence resolution, not to each empty source.

findings.title: Enumerate recognized enablement values
findings.body: AC18 says the recognized on/off values are the same vocabulary as the existing durability-mode switch but leaves the exact values to the plan. The allowed values are needed to test unrecognized-value handling and operator configuration. List the accepted values or incorporate the exact existing vocabulary by reference.

findings.title: Clarify AC1 surface rule for failures after publication
findings.body: AC1 says the check-run output carries the per-category record only when the pass's own check-run write produced a check run whose outcome is a review, but for failures after the review is public it says the record is on the logs 'in either case' while also referring to whatever per-category surface the write produced. The pass-outcome matrix repeats the ambiguity. State exactly which surfaces are required when a public review exists and the check-run write succeeds, partially fails, or never lands.

findings.title: Define reached categories without prescribing request internals
findings.body: AC1 defines a category as reached when 'the review request the pass issued carried it'. This makes the terminal-failure record depend on internal request composition rather than observable pass state. Define reached categories in observable terms (for example, categories recorded before failure) so the rule is testable without prescribing model-call design.

findings.title: Include controls in human-recorded miss adjudication
findings.body: AC15(b), Use Case 6, and the business rule say a clean head with a human-recorded defect is terminally adjudicated when that defect is recorded as a confirmed miss for both the sweep-enabled review and the external reviewer. Elsewhere a recorded sweep-off control is a compared reviewer. When a control exists, state whether the human-recorded defect must also be a confirmed miss for the control and how that affects terminal adjudication and recall.

findings.title: Make category-membership decisions testable
findings.body: AC15(d) says a defect is within the sweep's claim by an objective match to categories and failure shapes, but it also says records only state the test's verdict and no recorded entry decides membership. No objective matching procedure, evidence standard, or tie-breaker is defined. Since membership determines the confirmed-defect denominator, this is not testable. Define the matching procedure or make membership an explicitly recorded adjudication decision.

findings.title: Define outcomes for overlapping compared findings
findings.body: The spec does not say how to assign terminal outcomes when the same defect is reported by multiple compared reviewers. For example, if sweep-enabled and sweep-off controls both report a defect the external reviewer missed, or if control and external report a defect the sweep missed, it is unclear whether the outcome is duplicate, ronda_only, ronda_miss, or some combination. Define the outcome mapping and counting rule for overlapping findings.

findings.title: Make cohort closure before visibility operable
findings.body: AC15(b), Use Case 6, and the business rule require the eligible cohort to be closed by a cutoff fixed in advance 'before any eligible pass's findings are visible', while eligible passes have already completed and normally publish reviews. As written this may be impossible or unverifiable. Define what visible means, how the cutoff is recorded, and how closure is achieved without selection bias.

findings.title: Define handling of pull requests after a closed cohort
findings.body: The spec defines a closed eligible cohort for the ten-pull-request count but does not say whether later sweep-enabled pull requests start a new cohort, when that cohort closes, or how counts are rebuilt after a demotion. This leaves ongoing tier promotion and restoration undefined.

findings.title: Define tier effects of adjudication corrections
findings.body: Evidence-tier transitions list list revision and newly recorded controls as causes for the counted pull requests falling below ten. They do not cover an adjudication being corrected, reopened, or changed to unclear after the tier was measured. Since terminal adjudication determines the count, define how such corrections affect the tier and any claims.

findings.title: Define unpublished matched sweep-off controls
findings.body: AC15(d) and Use Case 6 require matched sweep-off controls on the same real-PR heads, recorded but not published, while the review contract maintains one review per head SHA. The spec does not define a non-publishing control pass, its record surfaces, or how it interacts with existing-check and supersede behavior. Without that, comparative recall/variance/cost evidence cannot be produced as written.

findings.title: Provide a fallback when the historical model is unavailable
findings.body: AC8 requires baseline comparability for the original-thirteen subset using the historical model and configuration held constant. It does not say what happens if the historical model is no longer available or the baseline cannot be reproduced. Define whether that subset comparison is then not applicable, replaced by a documented substitute, or omitted.

findings.title: Define unexpected findings for precision fixtures
findings.body: AC9 and Use Case 4 require counting unexpected findings and reporting whether each precision fixture stayed clean, but they do not define expected findings for precision fixtures that are not expected to be clean, or whether any finding on a clean fixture is automatically unexpected. Define the expected-finding contract for precision fixtures.

findings.title: Define run-position pairing for benchmark cost
findings.body: AC11 pairs benchmark runs by run position within each configuration's identical run sequence, but does not define how run positions are assigned or whether runs must be interleaved. Define the ordering rule so the paired cost metric is reproducible.

findings.title: Stabilize matrix mirror references
findings.body: The decision-gate consistency matrix cites mirror surfaces with approximate line numbers such as ~106, ~120, and ~541, and some references point to sections that do not own the rule (for example, AC16 for evidence-tier transitions). Replace line-number references with stable section or AC references and correct the mirrors.

findings.title: Clarify default-enablement gating wording
findings.body: The business rule says 'only two tests are gating' for the later default-enablement decision, then lists recall, variance, precision, and cost evidence plus no precision regression. Reword the rule to state the exact gating conditions without the conflicting count.

findings.title: Record each never-found kind separately
findings.body: AC6 says the excluded entries are the seeded benchmark's four never-found kinds, but Statuses / Enum Values records them as one grouped bullet. For traceability and candidate accounting, list each never-found kind as its own excluded candidate with the same rationale.

findings.title: Make log visibility wording conditional
findings.body: Operational Visibility says logs record that the sweep ran and the list version, but AC18 and AC19 require logs to carry unrecognized-enablement or sweep-did-not-run records, sometimes with no list version. Reword the log surface to cover all sweep-related records rather than implying a successful sweep run always occurred.

findings.title: Add missing Document Quality Gate log and Matrix coherence preflight
findings.body: The PR description is absent, so there is no current Document Quality Gate log. The checklist requires this log for spec PRs. Because the spec contains stateful constructs such as evidence-tier transitions and a decision-gate consistency matrix, the log should also include a Matrix coherence preflight row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable. Add the log to the PR description.

findings.title: Define per-category values for publication failures after the finding result exists
findings.body: AC1 says not determined applies when a terminal failure leaves the finding result unestablished, and ordinary produced-findings/produced-none values apply when the review is already public. It does not state what values are recorded when the failure occurs after the finding result exists but before publication, such as a failed review-publication call. Clarify whether such a pass records ordinary produced-findings/produced-none or not determined.

findings.title: Clarify check-run surface for terminal failures after a public review
findings.body: AC1 states the check-run output carries the per-category record only when the pass's own check-run write produced a check run whose outcome is a review. The later public-review failure paragraph says the record is on the logs in either case and with whatever per-category surface the check-run write produced. State explicitly whether the record also appears on the check-run output when a success check run whose outcome is a review exists.

findings.title: Define the recorded-but-unpublished sweep-off control artifact
findings.body: AC15(d) and Use Case 6 require matched sweep-off controls on real pull request heads that are recorded but not published. AC2 requires publication whenever the existing review flow reaches publication and preserves one review per head SHA. The spec does not define a non-publishing control pass, its record surfaces, or how its findings enter adjudication without violating the one-review-per-head contract. Add an explicit contract or exception for these control runs.

findings.title: Anchor precision-evidence pairing for real-PR recall claims
findings.body: AC15(d) requires AC9 precision evidence on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count for a real-pull-request recall claim, but real-pull-request claims do not have a fixture target or fixture version. Clarify whether this means a separate fixture-based precision comparison using the same model, category-list version, effective sweep configuration, and sample count, and how the precision target and fixture version are selected.

findings.title: Specify terminal outcome for rejected findings raised by both Ronda and external reviewer
findings.body: The adjudication outcomes section says ronda_better applies only to external-only findings and that rejected or out-of-scope findings raised by both Ronda and the external reviewer use the Ronda finding rejected outcome. However, the ronda_rejected description only covers findings reported by Ronda. State how the external reviewer's matching finding is recorded and made terminal in this case to avoid using one outcome with two meanings.

findings.title: Clarify whether terminally failed sweep passes count as sweep-enabled reviews
findings.body: The business rules define a sweep-enabled review as a review whose pass actually ran the sweep and reported a category list version. AC1 allows passes that reach review execution, run the sweep, and then fail terminally before publishing a review. The evidence-tier and ten-pull-request counts depend on pull requests carrying a sweep-enabled review. State whether such terminally failed passes promote the tier or count toward the ten, and if not, state that explicitly.

findings.title: Define aggregation of model calls and elapsed time per pass for multi-head runs
findings.body: AC11 and Use Case 4 require model calls per pass and elapsed time per pass, paired by run position, but benchmark runs can cover multiple heads or passes. The spec does not say whether a run's per-pass figure is a sum, mean, median, or another reduction across the passes in that run. AC15(d) also reduces per-head figures across repeated runs. Define the aggregation rules for these cases so cost claims are testable.

findings.title: Provide row-level evidence sources for initial categories
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values says the evidence source names the corpus rows behind each category, but the initial category table mostly records only The 2026-09-23 real-PR corpus. Add row identifiers, a stable pointer to the recorded corpus rows, or another explicit source reference so AC4's evidence-traceability requirement can be checked.

findings.title: Name the four excluded never-found seeded kinds individually
findings.body: AC6 requires excluded candidates to be named with their rationale. The excluded candidates list records The seeded benchmark's four never-found kinds as a group, while Use Case 2 names the four kinds. List each excluded never-found kind in the recorded list section so the candidate accounting is explicit.

findings.title: Add missing Document Quality Gate log
findings.body: The PR description is absent, so there is no current Document Quality Gate log. Because the spec adds decision gates and stateful evidence-tier transitions, the log must include a Matrix coherence preflight row or a reasoned Not applicable. Add the gate log before approval.

findings.title: Scope AC6 to the initial category list
findings.body: AC6 says the swept list holds exactly the five categories in Statuses / Enum Values, while Use Case 2, AC7, and the Business Rules allow later revisions that add or remove categories. As written, any revised current list violates AC6. Limit AC6 to the initial list version or to the initial candidate-set audit.

findings.title: Fix impossible precision-evidence pairing for real-PR recall claims
findings.body: AC15(d) and the Claim admissibility gate require AC9 precision evidence on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count as the real-pull-request comparison. AC9 and Use Case 4 define precision evidence as fixture runs, so it cannot share the real PR heads or their fixture version. Clarify the pairing requirement or define real-PR precision fixtures.

findings.title: Define non-publishing measurement mode for real-PR controls and repeated runs
findings.body: AC15(d) requires matched sweep-off controls and repeated variance runs on the same real pull request heads, but AC2 and the Business Rules preserve one review per head SHA and existing-check skip. Only benchmark runs are defined as publishing nothing. Define how real-PR control and repeated measurement runs are recorded without publishing, being skipped, or creating a second review.

findings.title: Assign surfaces for sweep-did-not-run and unrecognized-enablement records in AC1
findings.body: AC18, AC19, and the Business Rules say sweep-did-not-run and unrecognized-enablement records are carried on the surfaces AC1 assigns, but AC1 only assigns the per-category record and does not state where these two records appear. Add explicit surface assignment or correct the references.

findings.title: Define whether degraded enabled passes are sweep passes
findings.body: AC3 and AC20 use sweep pass, while AC18 and AC19 require passes with unrecognized enablement or unreadable lists to run as ordinary non-sweep reviews and report no list version. If those passes are sweep passes, AC3 and AC20 conflict; if not, the term needs a clear boundary. Define sweep pass and apply it consistently.

findings.title: Require category-list version consistency in AC8 recall evidence
findings.body: AC8 requires same target, model, fixture version, configuration, and sample count for benchmark recall runs, but it does not require the sweep-on runs to record or hold the category-list version constant. AC9 does this for precision. Add the category-list version to AC8 so recall comparisons are reproducible.

findings.title: Define cost aggregation when a run contains multiple passes
findings.body: AC11 and Use Case 4 pair per-run model calls per pass and elapsed time per pass, while Use Case 3 defines a run as covering a whole head set. The spec does not say how multiple passes inside one run are reduced to the per-run figure used for pairing. Define the aggregation rule.

findings.title: Define conflict resolution for category membership across repeated runs
findings.body: AC15(d) says claim membership is a cohort-level decision and that a pass record entry governs, but repeated runs can publish different findings or category entries. The spec does not say which entry or adjudication resolves conflicting membership for the same underlying defect. Define the conflict rule.

findings.title: Require one category-list version for a real-PR comparative claim
findings.body: AC15(d) reads claim membership against the list version each pass recorded, but it does not require all runs in a comparative claim to use the same list version. If the list is revised between runs, confirmed-defect membership and recall can change. Require a fixed list version for the comparative evidence or define the handling.

findings.title: Define where and how the cohort cutoff is recorded
findings.body: AC15(b) and Use Case 6 close the eligible cohort by a recorded cutoff, but no section defines the cutoff surface, format, time basis, or how it relates to review timestamps. Define the cutoff record so cohort selection is testable.

findings.title: Define terminal adjudication for human-recorded defects with no compared finding
findings.body: AC15(d) includes defects recorded only by human adjudication in the confirmed-defect denominator, but terminal adjudication is defined through outcomes on compared findings. State what outcome or record makes such a pull request terminal and how it interacts with clean-result confirmation.

findings.title: Define duplicate and underlying identity matching rule
findings.body: AC15(d) collapses duplicate outcomes by underlying identity and matches findings to confirmed defects, but it does not define how defect identity is established across reviewers, configurations, and repeated runs. Define the matching rule or cite the exact dependency contract rule.

findings.title: Define unexpected finding for precision fixtures
findings.body: AC9 and Use Case 4 count unexpected findings and decide precision regression from clean/not-clean fixture results, but they do not define what a precision fixture expects beyond a clean result. Without an expected-finding contract, the precision test is not testable.

findings.title: Enumerate recognized on/off values or cite the exact source
findings.body: AC18 refers to the existing durability-mode on/off vocabulary but does not enumerate the recognized values, and it defers exact values to the plan. List the allowed values or cite the exact existing contract so enablement resolution is testable.

findings.title: Clarify model-credential failure classification in AC1
findings.body: AC1 treats a model credential rejected by the model API as a failure after review execution, but such a failure could occur before changed files are read. Tie the classification to the observable before/after changed-files boundary rather than the credential error type.

findings.title: Define pass completed by a recorded cutoff
findings.body: Use Case 6 and AC15(b) count pull requests whose pass completed by a recorded cutoff or that carried a sweep-enabled review, but they do not say whether completion means review execution, publication, or a successful pass, nor how failed sweep passes are treated. Define the counting event.

findings.title: Define cohort state when a later control reopens adjudication
findings.body: The evidence-tier transitions allow a sweep-off control recorded after a measured cohort to drop the counted total, but they do not say whether the cutoff changes, how the cohort is re-closed, or whether newly eligible pull requests enter. Define the cohort lifecycle for reopened adjudications.

findings.title: Define the descriptive sweep-enabled miss record
findings.body: Use Case 6 and AC15(d) require a descriptive sweep-enabled miss record when no comparative control exists, but no acceptance criterion defines its fields, surface, or retention. Define the record so the descriptive claim is testable.

findings.title: Remove restated outcome code values from AC15(d) or amend the only-site claim
findings.body: Statuses / Enum Values says it is the only site that fixes the ronda_only and ronda_rejected code values, but AC15(d) restates those code values. Either remove the code values from AC15(d) or change the only-site statement.

findings.title: Define how adjudications record the swept category
findings.body: AC15(d) requires adjudications for external findings and human-recorded defects to name the swept category used for claim membership, but no status, field, or surface defines where that category is recorded. Define the adjudication category record.

findings.title: Resolve precedence between environment and workflow input in AC18
findings.body: AC18 says environment or workflow input outrank the operator config file, but it does not say which of environment and workflow input wins when both supply non-empty values. Define the full precedence order for enablement resolution.

errorMessage: Model request was aborted before it completed

findings.title: Add Document Quality Gate log with Matrix coherence preflight
findings.body: The PR description is absent, so the required current Document Quality Gate log is missing. Because the plan contains a decision-gate matrix and evidence-tier transition rules, the log must also include a Matrix coherence preflight row with the six-check audit summary or a reasoned Not applicable.

findings.title: Add plan-authoring rigor outcome record
findings.body: The plan does not contain the required plan-authoring rigor block naming Rules 1 through 6 by canonical name, the three outcome labels, the canonical rules link, and a per-rule outcome record with repository-derived evidence. A missing outcome record is blocking; add the block with evidence recorded at the plan revision.

findings.title: Align degraded-record emission boundary with the spec
findings.body: run-review-pass steps 1 and 2, Testing Strategy scenario 5, the Code Samples, and smoke-test Step 5 hold unrecognized-enablement and sweep-did-not-run records until the model review request is issued. Spec AC18 and AC19 require those degraded records from a pass that reaches review execution, and AC1 treats failures after the changed files are read as reaching review execution. A failure after changed-file reads but before the model request would still owe the degraded record under the spec. Fix the plan and runbook boundary or obtain a spec correction.

findings.title: Correct AC1 assertion for terminal failures
findings.body: The Assertions Checklist AC1 item says terminal failures after the request record not_determined on the logs only. Step 6 and the spec also require ordinary produced_findings or produced_none outcomes when the failure occurs after the review is already public. Rewrite the assertion to distinguish pre-publication and post-publication terminal failures.

findings.title: Resolve AC17 statement location conflict

Without a named baseline, the requirement is not testable. Identify the baseline evidence source or define the exact model/configuration set.

findings.title: Make precision-evidence pairing for real-PR recall claims coherent
findings.body: AC9 defines precision evidence over precision fixtures, but AC15(d) and the claim-admissibility matrix require that same precision evidence to be on the same target, model, fixture version, and sample count as a real-pull-request recall claim while also matching the real PR heads' model identity. A real-PR claim and a fixture precision run cannot share the same target/fixture in that reading. Clarify whether benchmark precision evidence backs real-PR recall claims, and if so state exactly which target/fixture/sample-count pairing applies.

findings.title: Define how real-PR controls and repeated runs are recorded without multiple reviews
findings.body: AC15(d) requires matched sweep-off controls and repeated identical real-PR runs for variance, while the review contract remains one review per head SHA. The spec says controls may be recorded but not published, but it never defines how such runs are triggered, recorded, kept unpublished, or associated with the head. Define the non-publishing evidence-capture path or remove the requirement.

findings.title: Specify where and how adjudications record swept-category membership
findings.body: AC15(d) requires membership decisions for confirmed defects to be recorded by naming the swept category for external findings, control findings, and human-only defects. The adjudication outcome enum and operational visibility surfaces do not define a category field, storage location, or record format. Add an explicit requirement for where this membership evidence is recorded and what values it may contain.

findings.title: Define outcomes for rejected or out-of-scope findings reported by both reviewers
findings.body: The spec defines 'duplicate' as a valid defect both reviewers found, 'ronda_better' for external-only rejected/out-of-scope findings, and 'ronda_rejected' for Ronda-reported rejected/out-of-scope findings. It does not define a terminal outcome for a finding reported by both Ronda and the external reviewer that adjudication later rejects as false positive or records as out of scope. Since every compared finding needs a terminal outcome, define the outcome or outcomes for this case.

findings.title: Specify defect identity and matching rules
findings.body: AC15(d) relies on 'the same defect as the adjudication records it', collapsing duplicates by underlying identity, but it does not define how defect identity is established, what evidence records the identity, or how adjudicators decide two findings are the same underlying issue. Add a testable matching rule or identify the record that carries the identity decision.

findings.title: Define how the eligible cohort cutoff is chosen
findings.body: Use Case 6 and AC15(b) require a closed eligible cohort defined by a recorded cutoff, but they do not say how the cutoff is selected or what prevents choosing a cutoff that excludes unfavorable eligible PRs. State an objective rule, such as including all eligible sweep-enabled PRs up to the claim date, or require recorded rationale and completeness evidence for the chosen cutoff.

findings.title: Define the descriptive sweep-enabled miss record
findings.body: The spec repeatedly requires a descriptive sweep-enabled miss record when no comparative claim is permitted, but it does not define the record's required fields, surface, or relationship to the evidence tier. Define what the miss record must contain and where it is stored so the requirement can be verified.

findings.title: Define 'sweep pass' consistently
findings.body: AC3 refers to a 'sweep pass' that publishes a review, while AC19 and Operational Visibility describe enabled passes that degrade to ordinary non-sweep reviews and still emit sweep-did-not-run records. Clarify whether a degraded enabled pass is a sweep pass, non-sweep pass, or a third state, and use the term consistently.

findings.title: Define run pairing keys for cost comparisons
findings.body: AC11 pairs benchmark cost runs by 'run position within each configuration's identical run sequence'. If run order is not part of the committed evidence, this pairing can be arbitrary. State the pairing key or evidence field, such as run index or timestamp pair, that makes the required pairing auditable.
